operations.description:
Search and filter shipment packages dispatched by sellers with comprehensive filtering and pagination.

Returns paginated shipment records matching search criteria including carrier name, tracking number, shipping dates, confirmation dates, delivery dates, and delivery status. Shipments represent physical delivery packages containing one or more order items from the same seller with shared carrier tracking information.

Role-based access control: Customers see only shipments related to their order history through joined order items and orders. Sellers see shipments they created by matching seller ID. Administrators see all platform shipments. Results optimized for list displays with essential tracking information, supporting pagination and sorting for large result sets.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_shipments table with filtering and pagination:

Authorization Logic:
- Customer: Filter shipments by joining ecommerce_platform_shipment_items to ecommerce_platform_order_items and matching to ecommerce_platform_orders where ecommerce_platform_customer_profile_id matches the authenticated customer
- Seller: Filter shipments by matching ecommerce_platform_seller_id to the authenticated seller
- Admin: Full access without restrictions

Query Pattern:
- carrierName: Partial case-insensitive match on carrier_name
- trackingNumber: Partial case-insensitive match on tracking_number
- shippedAfter: Filter where shipped_at is after the specified DateTime
- shippedBefore: Filter where shipped_at is before the specified DateTime
- confirmedAfter: Filter where confirmed_at is after the specified DateTime
- confirmedBefore: Filter where confirmed_at is before the specified DateTime
- deliveredAfter: Filter where delivered_at is after the specified DateTime
- deliveredBefore: Filter where delivered_at is before the specified DateTime
- status: Filter status as 'shipped' when confirmed_at IS NULL or 'delivered' when confirmed_at IS NOT NULL
- Exclude soft-deleted records: deleted_at IS NULL

Sorting:
- Default: shipped_at descending (newest first)
- Allow alternative: shipped_at, confirmed_at, delivered_at, carrier_name, tracking_number

Pagination:
- Cursor-based with limit (default 20, max 100)
- Return cursor token in response for next page

Join ecommerce_platform_shipment_items for order item count summary

Response Projection:
- id: Shipment identifier
- carrier_name: Carrier information
- tracking_number: Package tracking number
- shipped_at: Dispatch timestamp
- confirmed_at: Manual confirmation timestamp
- delivered_at: Delivery completion timestamp
- created_at: Record creation timestamp
- order_item_count: Count of order items in shipment

Performance Considerations:
- Indexes: carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, confirmed_at, delivered_at
- Apply filters before projecting from junction tables

responseBody.description: Paginated shipment summary records with tracking and delivery information. Each summary includes the shipment identifier, carrier name, tracking number, shipping timestamp, confirmation timestamp, delivery completion timestamp, creation timestamp, and order item count for shipment content overview. Results optimized for list display with role-based filtering applied based on authenticated user permissions.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for browsing shipment packages with role-based access control. Includes carrier name partial matching (case-insensitive), tracking number partial lookup (case-insensitive), date range filters for shipping (shippedAfter, shippedBefore), confirmation (confirmedAfter, confirmedBefore), and delivery dates (deliveredAfter, deliveredBefore), delivery status filtering (shipped, delivered), pagination parameters (limit, cursor), and sorting options (shipped_at, confirmed_at, carrier_name, tracking_number). Defaults to newest shipped_at for relevant user role contexts.

operations.rationale:
As a list/search endpoint with complex filtering requirements, PATCH is the correct HTTP method per the compiler-enforced constraint that 'index' name requires 'patch' method. GET cannot be used because the request body needs complex search filters.

The operation follows standard pagination patterns using cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Filtering is implemented through the request body to support various search criteria including partial matches on carrier name and tracking number, date range filtering for shipping/confirmation/delivery dates, and status filtering.

The response type IPageIEcommercePlatformShipment.ISummary follows naming conventions with the IPage prefix for paginated results. The IRequest type for search criteria provides flexibility for various search scenarios.

Role-based access control is implemented through authorization logic that filters results based on the authenticated user's role, ensuring data isolation and privacy compliance.

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information for a specific shipment by its unique identifier.

Returns the shipment's carrier name, tracking number, and shipping timeline including dispatched date, manual delivery confirmation date, and effective delivery date. The response includes all order items bundled in the shipment through the shipment items junction table, enabling customers to track package contents and sellers to verify fulfillment status.

Delivery confirmation operates at the shipment level: when a customer confirms receipt, all items in that shipment transition to delivered status together. If not manually confirmed, the system automatically marks the shipment as delivered after fourteen days from the shipping date.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_shipments table using the shipmentId UUID parameter on the id primary key column.

Filter:
- Exclude soft-deleted records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL.

Include relations:
- Join ecommerce_platform_sellers through ecommerce_platform_seller_id foreign key to include seller identity information
- Join ecommerce_platform_shipment_items through shipmentItems has-relation to include all bundled order items

Return fields from ecommerce_platform_shipments: id, ecommerce_platform_seller_id, carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, confirmed_at, delivered_at, created_at, updated_at

Error handling:
- Return 404 Not Found if no shipment exists with the given UUID
- Return 404 Not Found if the shipment is soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
- Validate UUID format in the path parameter

responseBody.description: Complete shipment details including carrier information, tracking number, shipping and delivery timestamps, and bundled order items.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment package to retrieve.
parameters.name: shipmentId

prerequisites.description: Shipment must exist before it can be retrieved by ID. POST /ecommercePlatform/seller/shipments creates the shipment record with carrier tracking information and bundled order items.

operations.description:
Create a new shipment by bundling order items and providing carrier tracking information.

This endpoint allows sellers to dispatch physical packages containing one or more order items. The seller provides the carrier name, tracking number, and selects which paid order items to include in this shipment package. Upon successful creation, all selected items transition to shipped status and share the tracking information in this package.

All order items must belong to products owned by the authenticated seller. Items from different sellers cannot be grouped into the same shipment. The carrier name and tracking number are immutable once the shipment record is created. If the seller only ships some available items, the system notes that remaining items require additional shipments.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
EXTRACT SELLER CONTEXT:
Obtain authenticated seller ID from middleware context.

VALIDATE REQUEST FIELDS:
- carrierName: non-empty string
- trackingNumber: non-empty string
- orderItemIds: non-empty array of UUID strings

UNIQUE TRACKING CHECK:
Query ecommerce_platform_shipments for @@unique([carrier_name, tracking_number]) match.
Reject with 409 Conflict if exists.

ITEM VALIDATION (per orderItemId):
1. Load ecommerce_platform_order_items row
2. Navigate: orderItem → productVariant → product → sellerProfile
3. Verify sellerProfile.id matches authenticated seller ID
4. Check orderItem.status == 'paid'
5. Check no existing record in ecommerce_platform_shipment_items for this orderItemId
Any failure returns 400 Bad Request.

ATOM TRANSACTION:
BEGIN
1. INSERT ecommerce_platform_shipments:
   seller_id = auth seller ID
   carrier_name = request.carrierName
   tracking_number = request.trackingNumber
   shipped_at = NOW()
   confirmed_at = null
   delivered_at = null

2. INSERT ecommerce_platform_shipment_items (per item):
   shipment_id = new shipment ID
   order_item_id = each validated orderItemId

3. UPDATE ecommerce_platform_order_items (per item):
   status = 'shipped'
   updated_at = NOW()

COMMIT
Return IEcommercePlatformShipment with nested shipmentItems joined through junction table to orderItems.

ERROR CONDITIONS:
400 - Cross-seller items, wrong status, duplicate assignments, empty fields
409 - Duplicate carrier+tracking combination

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment record with carrier tracking details, shipping timestamp, delivery timestamps (initially null), and all associated order item information.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation details including carrier name, tracking number, and the list of order item identifiers to bundle into this physical package.

prerequisites.description: Order items must exist with paid status before they can be bundled into a shipment. Order items are created during customer checkout when an order is placed.

operations.description:
Update a shipment record with carrier and tracking information.

Shipment tracking information is immutable after creation. Any attempt to modify the carrier name or tracking number will be rejected by the system, maintaining the original values as specified in business rules. This operation validates seller ownership and shipment existence before processing.

Shipment delivery status transitions are managed through dedicated delivery confirmation flows (customer confirmation or 14-day auto-delivery) rather than direct shipment updates. Sellers can only create shipments for their own order items, and each order item belongs to exactly one shipment.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_shipments table for the shipment by UUID primary key.

Validate that the authenticated seller is the owner of the shipment (ecommerce_platform_seller_id must match the authenticated seller's ID).

Reject the update if: 1) carrier_name differs from stored value, 2) tracking_number differs from stored value. Per Section 349, carrier name and tracking number are immutable once a shipment is created.

Reject the update if: shipment has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null), shipment does not exist (404), or shipment belongs to a different seller (403).

Return the unmodified shipment resource with all current field values. The shipment records the shipping timestamp (shipped_at), delivery confirmation timestamp (confirmed_at when customer manually confirms), and auto-delivery timestamp (delivered_at set by system 14 days after shipped_at if not manually confirmed).

responseBody.description: The shipment record with carrier name, tracking number, shipping date, and delivery confirmation status after the update operation.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment to update (UUID format).
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: Update request for shipment tracking information. Carrier name and tracking number modifications are rejected per immutability business rules.

prerequisites.description: Shipment must be created before its tracking information can be validated or updated by the seller.

operations.description:
Soft-deletes a seller's shipping package by marking it as deleted while preserving all tracking information and order item associations indefinitely.

Shipment deletion uses soft-deletion semantics to permanently preserve all audit trail evidence as required by platform policies. The operation sets the deleted_at timestamp without physical removal or data destruction.

Carrier names, tracking numbers, delivery confirmation timestamps, shipping dates, and all junction table mappings to order items remain immutable and permanently accessible for administrative auditing and dispute resolution.

Only the original seller who created the shipment is authorized to perform this operation. The authenticated seller's identity must match the ecommerce_platform_seller_id on the shipment record.

The endpoint returns the complete shipment entity reflecting the new deleted_at marker, enabling UI layers to confirm deletion state while maintaining full data integrity.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_shipments table filtering by id path parameter. Verify the authenticated actor's seller UUID matches ecommerce_platform_seller_id on the record. If mismatched, reject the request with an authorization error.

The operation implements soft deletion by updating the deleted_at column: if null, set it to the current timestamp; if already non-null, treat as idempotent (previously soft-deleted).

All fields except deleted_at remain immutable during this operation: carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, confirmed_at, delivered_at, created_at, updated_at. The junction table ecommerce_platform_shipment_items is NOT modified, cascaded, or severed. All included order items retain their shipment associations regardless of this soft deletion.

Return the complete IEcommercePlatformShipment entity representing the soft-deleted state with the populated deleted_at marker.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the shipping package to soft-delete. The resource must belong to the authenticated seller.
parameters.name: shipmentId

prerequisites.description: Shipment must be created before it can be soft-deleted

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order items contained in a specific shipment package.

This endpoint returns shipment item records that map order items to their parent shipment, sharing carrier name, tracking number, and shipping date. Each shipment is created by a seller to bundle multiple order items from the same seller into a single physical package for delivery.

The response includes item identifiers, order item references, and timestamps. Customers use this to track what items are included in a shipment they are waiting for. Sellers use this to verify which items are grouped in a shipment they dispatched.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_shipment_items table filtered by ecommerce_platform_shipment_id equal to the provided shipmentId parameter.

Apply pagination from request body (page number, page size). Count total matching records for pagination metadata.

Optionally join with ecommerce_platform_order_items on ecommerce_platform_order_item_id to include order item details (quantity, price, status).

Optionally join with ecommerce_platform_product_variants through order items for variant information.

Return paginated IPageIEcommercePlatformShipmentItem.ISummary containing matched shipment item records with summary fields.

Handle edge case where shipmentId does not exist by returning empty paginated result set (no items match).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment item summary records showing which order items are included in the specified shipment.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the shipment package (scoped to global shipment registry).
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: Search criteria including pagination parameters (page number, page size) for retrieving shipment items within the specified shipment package.

prerequisites.description: Shipment must be created before its items can be listed. The shipmentId path parameter references a shipment that must exist for meaningful results.

operations.description:
Retrieves a specific shipment item record that associates an order item with its corresponding shipment package.

Returns the junction record details including both foreign key references to the parent shipment and order item, along with audit timestamps tracking when the association was created and last modified. This endpoint enables customers to view the specific order item's inclusion in a shipment and sellers to verify a particular item's assignment to a delivery package.

Returns 404 NOT FOUND when the shipment item record does not exist, or when the shipment item does not belong to the specified parent shipment as validated by the ecommerce_platform_shipment_id foreign key constraint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_shipment_items table filtering by the primary key id matching the shipmentItemId path parameter.

Validate that the found record's ecommerce_platform_shipment_id foreign key matches the shipmentId path parameter to ensure the shipment item belongs to the specified parent shipment. Return 404 NOT FOUND if no record matches or if the parent-child relationship validation fails.

Verify the referenced shipment exists in ecommerce_platform_shipments table by checking the ecommerce_platform_shipment_id matches a valid shipment id.

Verify the referenced order item exists in ecommerce_platform_order_items table by checking the ecommerce_platform_order_item_id matches a valid order item id.

Return the complete shipment item entity containing all fields: id, ecommerce_platform_shipment_id, ecommerce_platform_order_item_id, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: The shipment item junction record containing the association between a shipment package and an order item. Includes foreign key references to parent shipment and order item, along with audit timestamps for when the mapping was created and last modified. No modifications are allowed on this entity through this endpoint.

parameters.description: UUID of the parent shipment package that contains this shipment item association.
parameters.name: shipmentId

parameters.description: UUID of the specific shipment item record that links an order item to a shipment package.
parameters.name: shipmentItemId

prerequisites.description: The shipment package must exist before order items can be added to it. Creates the parent resource with carrier name, tracking number, and dispatch information. Without an existing shipment, the order item cannot be bundled.
The shipment item junction record must be created by adding order items to the shipment. This POST creates the linking record between the shipment and the specific order item that is being retrieved.

operations.description:
Adds one or more order items to an existing shipment, bundling them into a single physical package for combined tracking.

All items in the shipment share the same carrier name, tracking number, and delivery confirmation status. Upon assignment, each order item's status transitions from 'paid' to 'shipped'.

Order items must belong to the same seller as the shipment, must be in 'paid' status, and cannot already be assigned to another shipment. Each order item can only belong to one shipment package. The operation is transactional — all items are added or none are.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the shipment record from ecommerce_platform_shipments by the shipmentId path parameter. Verify the shipment exists, is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL), and belongs to the authenticated seller's account.

2. Query ecommerce_platform_order_items for the order item IDs provided in the request body. For each order item:
   - Verify the item's product variant belongs to the same seller as the shipment (trace via product_variant → product → seller relationship).
   - Verify the item's status is 'paid' (not 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded').
   - Verify the item is not already assigned to another shipment by checking ecommerce_platform_shipment_items for an existing record with this order_item_id.

3. If all validations pass, create ecommerce_platform_shipment_items junction records within a single database transaction:
   - For each order item, INSERT a new record with shipment_id (from path), order_item_id (from request), and timestamps (created_at/updated_at).
   - UPDATE each order item's status from 'paid' to 'shipped'.
   - Set the shipment's shipped_at timestamp to current time if not already set.

4. If any validation fails, abort the entire transaction and return an error with details about which items failed validation.

5. Return the created shipment item records.

Edge cases:
- Reject empty orderItemIds array.
- Reject if any item belongs to a different seller.
- Reject if any item is already in 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded' status.
- Reject if any item is already assigned to an existing shipment.

responseBody.description: Array of shipment item records representing the created linkages between the shipment and the added order items.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment to add order items to.
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: Collection of order item identifiers to add to the existing shipment. Each order item must belong to the same seller as the shipment, must be in 'paid' status, and must not already be assigned to another shipment.

prerequisites.description: A purchase order must be created by the customer to generate the order items in 'paid' status that can be bundled into a shipment. The order provides the transactional line items referencing product variants and seller ownership.

A shipment record must be created by the seller to establish the parent package for tracking information. The shipment must exist before order items can be added to it to share carrier and tracking details.

operations.description:
Create a cancellation request for a specific order item. The customer submits an individual item cancellation request, providing the order item identifier and a reason for the cancellation request.

This operation is restricted to order items that have reached 'paid' status but have not yet been shipped. The system validates eligibility by checking the order item's current status, confirming no active shipment exists, ensuring the customer owns the item, and verifying no pending cancellation request already exists for that item.

Once created, the cancellation request enters a 'pending' state and awaits seller review. The seller will subsequently approve or reject the request through a separate operation. The system automatically records the customer from the authenticated session, so the request body only requires the target order item and cancellation reason.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract authenticated customer ID from the session context.

2. Query ecommerce_platform_order_items:
   - Verify the order item exists (by request body orderItemId).
   - Verify the order item belongs to the authenticated customer by joining ecommerce_platform_orders on orderId and checking orders.customerId matches the session customer.
   - Verify the order item status is exactly 'paid'. Reject with 400 if status is 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded'.

3. Check ecommerce_platform_shipments via ecommerce_platform_shipment_items:
   - Reject with 400 if any active shipment record contains this order item.

4. Check ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests:
   - Enforce @@unique constraint on ecommerce_platform_order_item_id.
   - Reject with 409 if any cancellation request already exists for this order item (regardless of status).

5. Insert into ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests:
   - id: generate UUID
   - ecommerce_platform_order_item_id: from request body
   - ecommerce_platform_customer_id: from authenticated session
   - reason: from request body
   - status: 'pending'
   - seller_response_reason: null
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp

6. Return the newly created cancellation request record with HTTP 201 status.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request record with status 'pending' and all system-generated fields populated.

requestBody.description: Cancellation request input including the target order item identifier and free-text cancellation reason.

prerequisites.description: The order containing the order item must be created first. Order items are generated atomically with the parent order during the checkout process. Without an existing order and its items, the `orderItemId` provided in the cancellation request would not exist.

operations.description:
Search and list cancellation requests with filtering and pagination support.

This endpoint retrieves a paginated list of cancellation requests, allowing filtering by status (pending, approved, rejected), customer, order item, date ranges, and other search criteria. Results are returned as summary records optimized for list displays.

Customers can view their own cancellation requests, sellers can view requests related to their products, and administrators have access to all cancellation requests on the platform.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests table with pagination and filtering capabilities.

Apply search filters based on the request body:
- status: filter by cancellation status (pending, approved, rejected)
- reason: text search on the cancellation reason field
- date ranges: filter by created_at or updated_at timestamps
- customer filters: filter by customer identity

For customers: restrict results to only their own requests using ecommerce_platform_customer_id.
For sellers: join through order_item -> product_variant -> product -> seller_product_profile to find requests for their products.
For admins: no additional restrictions.

Join with ecommerce_platform_order_items to include order item information in results if requested.
Return cursor-based or offset-based pagination based on system configuration.

Sort results by created_at descending by default (most recent first).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cancellation request summary records containing essential information for list display, including request status, customer details, and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for cancellation requests, including status filters, text search on reason, date range filters, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single cancellation request by its unique identifier.

Cancellation requests allow customers to request cancellation of order items that have 'paid' status before shipping. The returned entity includes the request reason, current processing status (pending, approved, or rejected), seller's response reason if rejected, and timestamps for creation and last update.

This endpoint supports both customer and seller access to cancellation request details for order management and dispute resolution workflows.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests table using the cancellationRequestId path parameter to retrieve a single cancellation request record.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the cancellationRequestId is a valid UUID format
2. Execute a SELECT query on ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests WHERE id = cancellationRequestId
3. Join with ecommerce_platform_order_items to include order item context
4. Join with ecommerce_platform_customers to include customer information
5. Return 404 if the cancellation request does not exist
6. Return 403 if the requesting user is not authorized to view this cancellation request
7. Return the cancellation request entity with all fields including id, ecommerce_platform_order_item_id, reason, status, seller_response_reason, created_at, updated_at

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: If no cancellation request exists with the provided ID
- 403 Forbidden: If the requesting user does not have permission to view this cancellation request
- Request authorization should verify the user is either the customer who created the request or the seller who owns the order item

responseBody.description: Full cancellation request entity containing request details, status, reason, and associated information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier for the cancellation request. Must be a valid UUID format.
parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

operations.description:
Updates a cancellation request by approving or rejecting it. Sellers respond to pending cancellation requests submitted by customers to either authorize the cancellation or deny it with an optional rejection reason. Only cancellation requests with 'pending' status can be modified. Upon approval, downstream processes trigger order item cancellation, inventory restoration, and refund processing. Upon rejection, the order item continues processing normally.

Cancellation requests are scoped per order item, ensuring only one request exists per item. The seller's response permanently records their decision in the request status field and optional seller_response_reason field.

Error handling includes rejecting updates to non-pending requests (approved or rejected status already) and enforcing that only sellers may respond to cancellation requests.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Find ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests by id (cancellationRequestId). Validate that the request exists and has status='pending'. If status is already 'approved' or 'rejected', reject with conflict error. Update the status field to either 'approved' or 'rejected' based on request body. If rejected, update seller_response_reason to the provided value (nullable). Set updated_at to current timestamp. On status change to 'approved', trigger transaction: query ecommerce_platform_order_items by ecommerce_platform_order_item_id, update its status to 'cancelled', restore inventory via ecommerce_platform_inventory_records for the product variant quantity, and initiate refund. For 'rejected' status, no downstream changes occur. Create snapshot in ecommerce_platform_snapshot_cancellation_requests and ecommerce_platform_snapshots for audit trail preservation. Return updated cancellation request entity.

responseBody.description: The updated cancellation request entity reflecting the seller's approval or rejection response with all current status and reason details.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cancellation request to update. UUID format matching the primary key of the cancellation request record.
parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

requestBody.description: Seller response containing the new status (approved or rejected) and optional rejection reason text when denying the cancellation request.

prerequisites.description: The cancellation request must be created before it can be updated by the seller.

operations.description:
Create a new refund request for a delivered order item.

Customers can submit refund requests for order items that have reached delivered status and were delivered within the seven-day refund window. The operation requires the order item identifier to refund and a textual reason explaining the refund request.

Upon submission, the refund request is created with a pending status and made available for the seller to review. The seller is automatically identified from the product chain and can subsequently approve or reject the request. The original order item and other items in the same order remain unaffected during the pending period.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Parse and validate the request body containing orderItemId and refundReason.

2. Verify the authenticated customer has ownership of the specified order item by checking the order_item's parent order's customer_profile_id matches the current customer.

3. Validate the order item status is 'delivered'. Reject with validation error if status is anything else (paid, shipped, cancelled, refunded).

4. Validate the 7-day refund window: check if the order item's updated_at (or the timestamp when status became 'delivered') is within 7 days of the current time. Reject with error if outside the window.
n5. Check for existing refund request on this order item via the unique constraint on order_item_id. Reject with conflict error if one already exists (pending, approved, or rejected).

6. Auto-populate seller_profile_id by traversing: order_item → product_variant → product → seller_profile.

7. Create the refund request record with:
   - order_item_id: from request
   - seller_profile_id: derived from product chain
   - refund_reason: from request
   - status: 'pending'
   - responded_at: null
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp

8. Create a snapshot record in ecommerce_platform_snapshot_refund_requests to capture the initial state.

9. Return the complete refund request entity in the response.

responseBody.description: The newly created refund request with pending status, including all fields populated including the auto-derived seller profile identifier.

requestBody.description: Refund request creation payload containing the order item identifier and customer-provided reason for the refund.

prerequisites.description: Order must be created first so that order items exist. The order item referenced by order_item_id must have been created as part of this order creation operation. Without an existing order item with delivered status, the refund request cannot be processed.

operations.description: Paginated collection of refund request summary records including status, reason, seller profile reference, and timestamps.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query ecommerce_platform_refund_requests table with pagination and filtering capabilities. Join with ecommerce_platform_seller_profiles when seller_profile_id filter is applied, and optionally join with ecommerce_platform_order_items for order item context. Apply the following filters: status (pending | approved | rejected), seller_profile_id (UUID), created_at date range, responded_at date range, and refund_reason text search. Enforce access control based on actor type: sellers can only see refund requests where seller_profile_id matches their profile; administrators can view all refund requests. Apply cursor-based pagination using IPage pattern. Sort by created_at descending by default. Return summary records containing id, order_item_id, seller_profile_id, refund_reason, status, responded_at, and created_at fields for efficient list display.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request summary records optimized for administrative and seller-facing list displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including status, seller profile ID, date ranges for created_at and responded_at fields, and text search on refund_reason field along with pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific refund request identified by its unique universal identifier.

Returns the complete refund request entity including the customer-provided refund reason, current approval status, seller response timestamp, and creation timestamps.

Use this endpoint to view the current state and details of any refund request in the system.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_refund_requests table to find a single record where the id matches the provided refundRequestId path parameter.

Return the complete refund request object including:
- id: Primary identifier
- order_item_id: Reference to the order item
- seller_profile_id: Reference to the seller processing this refund
- refund_reason: Text explanation provided by customer
- status: Current state (pending, approved, or rejected)
- responded_at: When seller responded (null if pending)
- created_at: When the request was submitted
- updated_at: Last modification timestamp

If no refund request exists with the given ID, return a 404 Not Found error.

Ensure UUID validation for the refundRequestId path parameter.

responseBody.description: Refund request details including reason, status, seller assignment, and timestamps.

parameters.description: Universal unique identifier of the refund request to retrieve
parameters.name: refundRequestId

prerequisites.description: The refund request must be created before it can be retrieved by ID

operations.description: Update a pending refund request by approving or rejecting it.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_refund_requests by id. Verify the request exists and is in 'pending' status, or reject with 409 Conflict if already approved/rejected.

Validate seller authorization: the authenticated seller must match the seller_profile_id on the refund request. If mismatch, return 403 Forbidden.

Check the order_item_id linked to the refund request:
- Join with ecommerce_platform_order_items to verify the item exists and has 'delivered' status.
- On approval: update order item status to 'refunded', process refund payment to the customer, create an inventory record in ecommerce_platform_inventory_records to restore stock for the product variant, compute and update parent order status (refunded if all items refunded, otherwise partially_completed).
- On rejection: keep order item status as 'delivered', no inventory changes.

Set refunded_at timestamp on the refund_request record. Compute updated_at. Create a snapshot entry via ecommerce_platform_snapshots and ecommerce_platform_snapshot_refund_requests to record the state transition.

Return 409 Conflict if refund request status is not 'pending'.

responseBody.description: Updated refund request record reflecting the seller's approval or rejection decision.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the refund request to respond to.
parameters.name: refundRequestId

requestBody.description: Seller's response decision to the refund request, including approval or rejection status and optional notes for the customer.

prerequisites.description: Order must be created to generate the order items that can later be refunded. Order items cannot exist independently.
Refund request must be created by the customer for a delivered order item before the seller can approve or reject it.

operations.description:
Search snapshots for a specific order item within a specific order.

This endpoint retrieves immutable snapshot records that preserve the transactional state of an order item at the time of purchase, including quantity and unit price. Snapshots are automatically generated by the system at order creation and cannot be modified or deleted by any user.

Customers can access snapshots of their own order items for order history verification and dispute resolution purposes. Snapshots preserve purchase-time details even if the product price or variant details change later.

Returns paginated results optimized for list displays and audit trail searches. This is a read-only operation - snapshots are system-generated and cannot be created, modified, or deleted through this API.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_snapshot_order_items joined with ecommerce_platform_snapshots to retrieve snapshots for the specified order item.

1. Validate orderId matches an existing order in ecommerce_platform_orders
2. Retrieve the target order item from ecommerce_platform_order_items where id equals itemId
3. Verify the order item belongs to the specified order (ecommerce_platform_order_id equals orderId)
4. Query ecommerce_platform_snapshot_order_items where ecommerce_platform_order_items_id equals itemId
5. Join with ecommerce_platform_snapshots on ecommerce_platform_snapshots_id to get header fields
6. Verify entity_type equals 'order_item' in the snapshots table
7. Apply any search filters and pagination from the request body
8. Return cursor-based pagination results

Validation:
- Return 404 if orderId does not match any order
- Return 404 if itemId does not match any order item
- Return 404 if the order item does not belong to the specified orderId
- Verify authenticated customer owns the order (ecommerce_platform_customer_profile_id matches)
- Snapshots are immutable - no write operations allowed
- System-generated data - only read access via index and at operations

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item snapshot summary records containing immutable historical state data (quantity, unit price, timestamp) for the specified order item.

parameters.description: UUID identifier for the parent order containing the order item
parameters.name: orderId

parameters.description: UUID identifier for the specific order item to retrieve snapshots for
parameters.name: itemId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for querying order item snapshot records, including date ranges and cursor-based pagination.

prerequisites.description: Order and order items must be created before snapshots can be queried. The checkout process creates the order record, generates order line items, and automatically creates immutable order item snapshots preserving quantity and unit price at purchase time.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific snapshot record for an order item, showing the quantity and unit price preserved at the moment of purchase.

This endpoint supports dispute resolution and historical auditing by providing customers, sellers, and administrators access to the exact transactional details that existed when the purchase was made. The snapshot data is immutable and independent of any subsequent price changes, inventory adjustments, or product modifications.

The snapshot preserves the quantity ordered and the unit price paid, as part of the permanent transaction record that is retained indefinitely according to platform data retention policy.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Verify the requested snapshot exists by joining `ecommerce_platform_snapshots` with `ecommerce_platform_snapshot_order_items` on the 1:1 relationship.
2. Verify the snapshot's `ecommerce_platform_order_items_id` matches the `itemId` path parameter, and the order item's `ecommerce_platform_order_id` matches the `orderId` path parameter. If mismatch, return 404 (the snapshot does not belong to the specified order item).
3. Apply authorization checks: customers can only access snapshots of orders belonging to their own customer profile; sellers can access snapshots of orders containing their products; admins have full access.
4. Return the combined snapshot data: header fields (id, entity_type, created_at) from `ecommerce_platform_snapshots` plus subtype fields (quantity, unit_price, created_at, updated_at) from `ecommerce_platform_snapshot_order_items`.
5. Ensure entity_type is 'order_item' to confirm the snapshot is for the correct entity type.

responseBody.description: The complete order item snapshot record including transactional details (quantity and unit price) preserved at the time of purchase.

parameters.description: UUID of the specific order item being snapshotted.
parameters.name: itemId

parameters.description: UUID of the snapshot record to retrieve.
parameters.name: snapshotId

prerequisites.description: The parent order must be created and the order item must exist; this operation triggers the automatic creation and immutably stores the targeted snapshot of the order item's transactional state at the time of purchase.

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated snapshots for a specific cancellation request. Each snapshot captures an immutable record of state changes including modifications to the cancellation reason and status over the request's lifecycle.

These snapshots provide historical evidence for dispute resolution by recording the complete audit trail showing what changed, when it changed, and the before/after values for mutable fields.

Snapshots are system-generated automatically when cancellation requests are modified and cannot be created, updated, or deleted by users including administrators.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_snapshot_cancellation_requests table filtered by the cancellationRequestId path parameter (ecommerce_platform_cancellation_request_id FK constraint).

Join with ecommerce_platform_snapshots to include entity_type and timestamp information from the polymorphic parent.

Apply pagination using cursor-based pagination for large result sets - extract offset/limit from request body.

Filter on entity_type = 'cancellation_request' to ensure only cancellation request snapshots are returned.

Return fields from ecommerce_platform_snapshot_cancellation_requests: id, cancellation_request_id, previous_reason, current_reason, previous_status, current_status, created_at, updated_at.

Return fields from ecommerce_platform_snapshots: entity_type, created_at timestamp.

Since snapshots are immutable, do NOT allow any modification operations. Validation should only filter/search criteria, not creation or modification of snapshot data.

Sort snapshots chronologically by created_at ascending to show evolution of the cancellation request over time.

Edge cases:
- Cancellation request does not exist → return appropriate error
- No snapshots exist for cancellation request → return empty results with pagination metadata
- Access restricted → enforce read-only, deny any modify operations
- Verify snapshot records link to valid cancellation request via FK

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cancellation request snapshot summary records showing historical state changes for dispute resolution and audit trail purposes

parameters.description: UUID of the cancellation request whose snapshots are being retrieved, used for filtering the snapshot records scoped to this specific request
parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for retrieving cancellation request snapshots including pagination controls and sorting preferences

prerequisites.description: The cancellation request must exist before its snapshots can be retrieved. The path parameter cancellationRequestId requires this entity, and the specification documents an error if it does not exist. Snapshots are automatically generated as the request is modified or created.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific cancellation request snapshot showing state transition details.

Returns immutable historical record capturing the before and after values of reason and status fields whenever a cancellation request changes state. Supports dispute resolution by providing verifiable proof of request modifications.

Access restricted to relevant parties: customers associated with the order item, sellers managing the cancellation request, and platform administrators with dispute resolution privileges.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query cancellation request snapshot retrieval.

1. Validate cancellationRequestId exists in ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests
2. Validate snapshotId exists in ecommerce_platform_snapshot_cancellation_requests
3. Verify ecommerce_platform_snapshot_cancellation_requests.ecommerce_platform_cancellation_request_id = cancellationRequestId
4. Join ecommerce_platform_snapshots header table on ecommerce_platform_snapshot_cancellation_requests.ecommerce_platform_snapshot_id = ecommerce_platform_snapshots.id
5. Filter by entity_type = 'cancellation_request'
6. Return single IEcommercePlatformSnapshotCancellationRequest entity with fields: id, ecommerce_platform_snapshot_id, ecommerce_platform_cancellation_request_id, previous_reason, current_reason, previous_status, current_status, created_at, updated_at
7. Authorize access: customer must own the related order item, or seller must be associated with the order, or admin has platform oversight

responseBody.description: Snapshot entity containing state transition details showing previous and current values of cancellation request reason and status fields, along with polymorphic entity type and creation timestamp.

operations.description:
Searches and retrieves a paginated list of snapshot records for a specific refund request. Snapshots are immutable audit trail records created automatically by the system whenever a seller responds to a refund request (approve or reject). Each snapshot captures the refund request state before and after the transition, including the refund reason and approval status changes.

This endpoint supports dispute resolution and audit requirements by providing transparent historical records of refund request lifecycle events. Access is restricted to relevant parties including the customer who submitted the refund request, the seller assigned to process it, and platform administrators for oversight purposes.

Snapshots cannot be created, modified, or deleted through API operations - they are system-generated records. This endpoint supports filtering by pagination parameters and status criteria.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the `ecommerce_platform_snapshot_refund_requests` table filtered by `ecommerce_platform_refund_requests_id` matching the provided `refundRequestId` path parameter.

Apply search filters from the request body including pagination parameters (cursor/limit), date range filters for `created_at`, and status filters for `previous_approval_status` or `current_approval_status`. Support text-based filtering on `current_reason` or `previous_reason` using the GIN trigram index on the parent refund_requests table.

Join with `ecommerce_platform_snapshots` if `entity_type` filtering is needed, though the child table contains all refund-request-specific fields.

Apply pagination using cursor-based strategy, ordered by `created_at` descending to show most recent snapshots first.

Enforce authorization checks: verify the requester is the customer associated with the refund request (via order_item_id → order_id relationship), the seller associated with the refund request (via seller_profile_id), or an administrator.

Never allow mutation operations on snapshots - this is strictly a read-only endpoint for audit trail access.

responseBody.description: Paginated result set of refund request snapshot summary records, ordered by creation timestamp descending with cursor-based pagination metadata.

parameters.description: UUID of the refund request whose snapshot records are being retrieved. Identifies the specific refund request lifecycle events to browse.
parameters.name: refundRequestId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering refund request snapshots, including date ranges, status filters, and cursor-based pagination settings.

prerequisites.description: Refund request must exist before its snapshot records can be queried. The refund request is the entity that triggers snapshot creation when state changes occur (approve/reject responses)

operations.description:
Retrieves a specific refund request snapshot record, providing the immutable before and after state values captured at the time of a refund request change.

This endpoint shows the previous and current values for the refund reason and approval status, enabling customers, sellers, and administrators to verify historical transaction states for dispute resolution. Snapshots are created automatically by the system when sellers respond to refund requests (approve or reject).

Accessible to the customer who created the refund request, the seller assigned to process it, and all administrators. The returned snapshot record is immutable and cannot be modified or deleted.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the polymorphic snapshot system to retrieve a specific refund request snapshot record.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate `refundRequestId` corresponds to an existing record in `ecommerce_platform_refund_requests`
2. Validate `snapshotId` exists in `ecommerce_platform_snapshot_refund_requests`
3. Verify the snapshot belongs to the specified refund request by checking `ecommerce_platform_refund_requests_id` matches `refundRequestId`
4. Return the full snapshot record joining `ecommerce_platform_snapshot_refund_requests` with `ecommerce_platform_snapshots`

Fields to return in IEcommercePlatformSnapshotRefundRequest:
- `id`: snapshot record primary key (UUID)
- `ecommerce_platform_snapshots_id`: FK to polymorphic snapshot header table
- `ecommerce_platform_refund_requests_id`: FK to the specific refund request
- `previous_reason`: customer's refund reason before the state change (nullable if first snapshot)
- `current_reason`: customer's refund reason after the state change
- `previous_approval_status`: approval status before the change (nullable if first snapshot)
- `current_approval_status`: approval status after the change (always present)
- `created_at`: timestamp when this snapshot was created

Edge cases:
- Return 404 if `refundRequestId` does not exist in `ecommerce_platform_refund_requests`
- Return 404 if `snapshotId` does not match any record in `ecommerce_platform_snapshot_refund_requests`
- Return 404 if `refundRequestId` does not match the snapshot's `ecommerce_platform_refund_requests_id`

Authorization:
- Customer who created the refund request can view its snapshots
- Seller assigned to process the refund request can view its snapshots
- Regular and super administrators can view all refund request snapshots

responseBody.description: Full refund request snapshot record containing previous and current state values for the refund reason and approval status at the time of the captured state change. Includes the immutable snapshot identifier, parent snapshot header reference, refund request reference, before and after values for reason and approval status, and creation timestamp.

parameters.description: UUID of the parent refund request that this snapshot belongs to (scoped to refund request).

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of products the authenticated customer has saved to their wishlist.

Returns wishlist entries with current product details including name, base price, and associated identifiers. Products deleted by sellers are automatically excluded from results, ensuring only available items appear. Each entry represents a product-level save without variant-specific configurations - customers express general interest in products regardless of specific options like color or size.

The wishlist prevents duplicate saves per product per customer. Customers can manage individual entries independently - removing one product does not affect other wishlist items or other customers' wishlists.

Supports cursor-based pagination for large result sets, with optional filtering by product name search and save date ranges. Results are optimized for customer-facing list views and wishlist browsing interfaces.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_wishlist_items filtered by authenticated customer ID from session. Only retrieve entries where deleted_at IS NULL.

Join ecommerce_platform_products for current product details. Exclude entries where product.deleted_at IS NOT NULL per section [457].

Retrieve fields: id as wishlistItemId, ecommerce_platform_product_id as productId, p.name as productName, p.base_price as productBasePrice, created_at as savedAt, updated_at.

Pagination: cursor-based or page/limit from requestBody.

Apply filters from requestBody:
- Product name substring search (case-insensitive) on p.name
- Date range filters on created_at (wishlist save timestamp)
- Sort order: created_at DESC (newest first) or name ASC (alphabetical)

Edge cases:
- Empty wishlist: return empty items array with total=0
- All products deleted: treated as empty, automatically excluded
- Customer auth validation: reject 401 if customer_id missing/invalid

Query pattern:
SELECT wi.id, wi.ecommerce_platform_product_id, p.name, p.base_price, wi.created_at, wi.updated_at
FROM ecommerce_platform_wishlist_items wi
JOIN ecommerce_platform_products p ON wi.ecommerce_platform_product_id = p.id
WHERE wi.ecommerce_platform_customer_id = :customerId
  AND wi.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
ORDER BY wi.created_at DESC;

Apply additional requestBody filters as WHERE conditions. Enforce pagination limits.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist item summaries featuring product identifiers, current product names, base pricing, and save timestamps. Excludes any entries where the associated product has been deleted. Optimized for customer-facing list displays and browsing interfaces.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for retrieving wishlist items including optional product name substring filter, save date range constraints, sort order preferences, and cursor or page-based pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Create a wishlist entry by saving a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This endpoint adds a product reference to the customer's personal wishlist, allowing them to track items of interest for future purchase consideration. The operation establishes a new association between the customer and product with automatic timestamp tracking.

Unique product constraint enforcement prevents duplicate entries — if a product is already in the customer's wishlist, the request is rejected. Only existing, non-deleted products can be added.

The authenticated customer's identity is automatically determined from the active session context, eliminating the need for explicit customer identification.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new record in the ecommerce_platform_wishlist_items table.

1. Extract ecommerce_platform_customer_id from the authenticated customer session
2. Validate the ecommerce_platform_product_id from the ICreate request body
3. Query ecommerce_platform_products to verify the product exists and is not soft-deleted
4. Check the composite unique constraint on (ecommerce_platform_customer_id, ecommerce_platform_product_id)
5. Insert new row with:
   - id: auto-generated UUID
   - ecommerce_platform_customer_id: from session
   - ecommerce_platform_product_id: from request
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: NULL

Error handling:
- 401 if unauthenticated
- 404 if product not found or soft-deleted
- 409 if the product already exists in the customer's wishlist

On success, return the complete ICreateResponse with populated product reference.

responseBody.description: Complete wishlist entry record including the product relationship populated with details.

requestBody.description: Product identifier to save to the authenticated customer's wishlist.

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before a customer can add it to their wishlist. The wishlist entry references the product via foreign key constraint that requires the product to exist and not be soft-deleted.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single wishlist item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint allows customers to view detailed information about a specific wishlist entry they have saved, including the associated product reference and metadata about when it was added and last modified. Returns the complete wishlist item record when the requesting customer is the owner.

Wishlist items represent product-level interest rather than specific variant configurations, meaning customers save entire products to their wishlist without committing to particular option combinations like color or size. This is distinct from shopping cart items, which reference specific product variants.

Returns 404 if the wishlist item does not exist or has been soft-deleted. Returns 403 if the requesting customer is not the owner of the wishlist item.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_wishlist_items table by primary key id matching wishlistItemId path parameter.

Validate that the wishlist item exists and has not been soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL).

Verify authorization by checking that ecommerce_platform_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID. The requesting customer must be the owner of the wishlist item.

Return the complete wishlist item record including all fields:
- id: unique identifier (UUID)
- ecommerce_platform_customer_id: reference to customer who saved the product
- ecommerce_platform_product_id: reference to the saved product
- created_at: timestamp when product was added to wishlist
- updated_at: timestamp when wishlist entry was last modified
- deleted_at: should be NULL for active entries

Validate that the referenced product (ecommerce_platform_product_id) exists in ecommerce_platform_products table, though cascade deletion automatically removes wishlist items when products are deleted.

Return 404 Not Found if:
- No wishlist item exists with the given id
- The wishlist item has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is not NULL)

Return 403 Forbidden if the authenticated customer is not the owner (ecommerce_platform_customer_id does not match customer ID).

responseBody.description: The complete wishlist item record containing the saved product reference, owner customer reference, and timestamp metadata.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the wishlist item to retrieve.
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

prerequisites.description: Wishlist item must exist before it can be retrieved by ID. The POST operation creates a wishlist entry linking a customer to a product, storing the product reference and timestamp metadata. Without this prerequisite, the GET would return 404 because the wishlist item record does not exist.

operations.description:
Removes a product from a customer's wishlist by performing a soft delete on the specified wishlist item.

This operation sets the deleted_at timestamp on the wishlist entry, effectively removing it from customer's paginated list view. The removal is immediate and permanent — no trash bin or undo history is provided. Removing a product from one customer's wishlist has no effect on that product's presence in other customers' wishlists or its availability on the platform.

Only the owner of the wishlist item can perform this removal. Attempting to remove an item that has already been deleted will result in a not-found error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_wishlist_items table for the wishlist item using the provided wishlistItemId as the id parameter where deleted_at IS NULL.

If the wishlist item does not exist or has already been soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), return 404 Not Found.

Validate that the authenticated customer is the owner by comparing their ID against the ecommerce_platform_customer_id field. If the IDs do not match, return 403 Forbidden.

Perform soft delete by updating the deleted_at field to the current timestamp (NOW()). Do not physically delete the row to preserve the audit trail.

Return 204 No Content with no response body on success.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the wishlist item to remove (global scope)
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

prerequisites.description: Wishlist item must be created before it can be removed via soft delete

operations.description:
Search product reviews with criteria filtering and pagination.

Returns paginated collection of reviews matching specified search filters. Reviews display customer feedback on products, including star ratings (1-5 scale) and optional text content. Reviews are sorted newest-first by default, consistent with product detail page display requirements.

Soft-deleted reviews are excluded from results by default, following business rules for average rating calculations and product evaluation visibility. Non-deleted reviews remain visible even after customer account deletion, attributed as 'deleted user'.

The response includes total count of non-deleted matching reviews.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_reviews table. Apply filtering on product_id, customer_id, order_id, rating range (1-5), text_content matches, created_at or updated_at date range filters.

WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted by default).

Default ORDER BY created_at DESC for newest-first sorting.

Paginated results using offset-based or cursor-based pagination.

JOIN with ecommerce_platform_customers to fetch display_name. When customer deleted_at IS NOT NULL, use 'deleted user'.

JOIN with ecommerce_platform_products for product context when needed.

Return paginated summary records.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary records including star rating, text content, product and customer context, sorted newest-first.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including product identifier filter, customer identifier filter, order identifier filter, rating range constraints, text content search, date range filters on created_at or updated_at timestamps, pagination parameters.

WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted by default).

operations.description:
Submit a product review with star rating and optional text content.

Authenticated customers can submit reviews for products purchased through completed orders. Reviews must include a mandatory star rating of 1-5 stars and may optionally include textual comments. The submission is validated to ensure the order has been delivered and the customer has not already reviewed this product.

Reviews become visible on product detail pages and contribute to the average rating calculation. If the reviewing customer deletes their account, reviews remain visible but the reviewer name displays as 'deleted user'. Customers may edit their reviews, creating preserved snapshots of previous states for audit purposes.

The endpoint automatically identifies the reviewer from their authentication session, requiring only the product identifier, order identifier, rating, and optional text content.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification:
Queries:
- Query ecommerce_platform_products WHERE id = requestBody.productId
- Query ecommerce_platform_orders WHERE id = requestBody.orderId AND status = 'delivered' AND ecommerce_platform_customer_id = customerId
- Query ecommerce_platform_order_items WHERE ecommerce_platform_order_id = orderId AND ecommerce_platform_product_id = productId
- Query ecommerce_platform_reviews WHERE ((ecommerce_platform_product_id = productId) AND (ecommerce_platform_customer_id = customerId)) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

Service logic:
1. Extract customer ID from authenticated session
2. Validate productId is a valid UUID
3. Validate orderId is a valid UUID
4. Validate rating is an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive
5. Optionally validate textContent is a valid string if provided
6. Verify the order belongs to the authenticated customer
7. Confirm at least one order item for the product has delivered status
8. Ensure no existing review exists for this customer and product (deleted_at IS NULL)
9. Create the review with the specified rating and text content
10. Set timestamp fields
11. Return the created review

Edge cases:
- Product not found
- Order does not belong to the customer
- Order does not contain a delivered product item
- Duplicate review already exists
- Rating is outside valid range

Error handling:
- 401: Not authenticated
- 404: Product not found
- 409: Review already exists for this product and order
- 412: Order item not delivered

responseBody.description: Complete review entity that includes the generated identifier, rating, text content, timestamps, and relationship references to product and order. The response confirms successful review submission.

requestBody.description: Review submission data that specifies the target product, order context, and review content. The customer is automatically identified from their authenticated session.

prerequisites.description: Product must exist before it can be reviewed. The product is created by an approved seller and must be listed in the marketplace with variants available for purchase. Reviews reference the product to contribute to its average rating calculation.

Order must exist before a review can reference it. The customer must complete checkout to create an order containing the purchased product variant. The order must reach 'delivered' status for the specific product item before review submission is permitted, establishing valid purchase history grounding the review in an actual transaction.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single review by its unique identifier.

Returns the complete review record including the star rating (1-5), optional text content, associated product information, and reviewer identity. Reviews submitted by users who have since deleted their accounts remain accessible and display 'deleted user' as the reviewer identity. This preserves the review's value for other customers making purchasing decisions while respecting the account deletion.

The review includes the timestamp of original submission and last update if the review has been edited by its author.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_platform_reviews table for the review with the matching id.

Join with ecommerce_platform_products to include product name and basic details in the response.
Join with ecommerce_platform_customer_profiles to get the reviewer's display name. If the customer profile's deleted_at is not null, return 'deleted user' as the reviewer identity instead of the display name.

Return a 404 error if no review exists with the given ID or if the review has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null). Deleted reviews should not be retrievable via this endpoint.

Validate that the reviewId is a valid UUID format before querying.

responseBody.description: Complete review record including star rating, optional text content, product information, and reviewer identity.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to retrieve (global scope).
parameters.name: reviewId

This preserves the review's value for other customers making purchasing decisions while respecting the account deletion.

The review includes the timestamp of original submission and last update if the review has been edited by its author.

operations.specification:

Join with ecommerce_platform_products to include product name and basic details in the response.
Join with ecommerce_platform_customer_profiles to get the reviewer's display name. If the customer profile's deleted_at is not null, return 'deleted user' as the reviewer identity instead of the display name.

operations.description:
Update an existing product review with a new star rating and optional text content.

Authenticated customers can modify their own reviews at any time. Each edit preserves a snapshot of the previous state for audit trail purposes. The star rating must be between 1 and 5, and the text content is optional.

Reviews can only be edited by their original author. The review must not have been previously deleted.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate the reviewId UUID and fetch the review from ecommerce_platform_reviews.
2. Verify the review exists and has not been soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
3. Verify the authenticated customer's ID matches the review's ecommerce_platform_customer_id field. Return 403 Forbidden if not the owner.
4. Validate the rating field is an integer between 1 and 5 (inclusive).
5. Validate text_content is either null or a valid string.
6. Before updating, create a snapshot record in ecommerce_platform_snapshots and ecommerce_platform_snapshot_reviews tables capturing the previous state (old rating, old text_content, old updated_at).
7. Update the review's rating and text_content fields.
8. Update the updated_at timestamp to the current time.
9. Return the updated review entity with all fields including the new rating, text_content, and updated_at timestamp.

responseBody.description: The updated review with the new star rating, text content, and updated timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review to update.
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Updated review content including the star rating (1-5) and optional text comment.

prerequisites.description: The review must be created before it can be updated. A review identified by reviewId must exist in the database with an active (non-deleted) state for the update operation to succeed.

operations.description:
Soft-delete a customer's review from the ecommerce platform.

When a customer deletes their review, the system first preserves a complete snapshot of the review's current state (star rating and text content) before applying the soft deletion. The review is marked as deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp, which excludes it from public visibility on product detail pages and removes it from the product's average rating calculation.

Only the customer who authored the review can delete it. Reviews remain attributed to deleted users when the customer account is removed, and the review data is preserved for platform integrity and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete the review referenced by reviewId.

1. Verify ownership: The authenticated customer must be the review author (ecommerce_platform_reviews.ecommerce_platform_customer_id matches auth context userId). Return 403 Forbidden if not the author.

2. Query ecommerce_platform_reviews by UUID. Return 404 Not Found if review doesn't exist or is already deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

3. Create audit snapshot before deletion:
   - Insert into ecommerce_platform_snapshots with entity_type='review'
   - Insert into ecommerce_platform_snapshot_reviews capturing:
     * previous_rating: current review rating
     * previous_content: current review text_content
     * new_rating: same as previous (state preserved)
     * new_content: same as previous
     * Link to both the new snapshot and this review

4. Soft-delete: Set deleted_at = current timestamp on the review record

5. Recalculate product's average rating:
   - Compute AVG(rating) from ecommerce_platform_reviews where:
     * ecommerce_platform_product_id matches the review's product
     * deleted_at IS NULL (only active reviews)
   - Update the product's cached/stored average rating

6. Return the deleted review entity with all fields including the new deleted_at timestamp for confirmation.

Edge cases:
- Already deleted review (deleted_at set): 404 Not Found
- Review from deleted customer account: Allow deletion by the account's remaining credentials if any, otherwise handle appropriately
- Concurrent deletion attempts: Use database constraints or optimistic locking to prevent duplicate operations

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to delete (global scope)
parameters.name: reviewId

prerequisites.description: Review must be created before it can be soft-deleted. The DELETE operation requires the review entity to exist in the database with a valid UUID identifier before setting the deleted_at timestamp. Returns 404 Not Found if the review doesn't exist.

operations.description:
Search and filter review snapshot records with pagination support.

Review snapshots are immutable audit trail entries automatically generated when customers edit or delete their reviews. Each snapshot preserves both the previous and current state of the review's star rating (1-5) and text content. These records provide verifiable historical data for dispute resolution and platform oversight.

Snapshots are sorted newest-first by default. Filters are available for review ID, entity type, date ranges, and content matching. Only read access is provided as snapshots are system-managed immutable records that cannot be modified or deleted by any user.

operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_platform_snapshot_reviews joined with ecommerce_platform_snapshots to retrieve review snapshot records.

- Filter ecommerce_platform_snapshots.entity_type = 'review'

Apply search filters from request body on:
- reviewId: filter by ecommerce_platform_snapshot_reviews.ecommerce_platform_review_id
- date range: filter by ecommerce_platform_snapshots.created_at
- Content/rating filters: previous_rating, new_rating, previous_content, new_content

Return cursor-based pagination using IPageIEcommercePlatformSnapshotReview.ISummary.
Default sort: created_at descending (newest first).

Snapshots are immutable - no write operations allowed. This is a read-only endpoint accessible by administrators for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

Handle cases where referenced reviews may have been deleted (customer deleted their own review).
