IEcommercePlatformCategory.description:
Complete category entity representing a product classification on the ecommerce platform, supporting a two-level hierarchy structure.

Categories organize products into root categories and subcategories. Root categories define primary classifications without a parent, while subcategories refine these primary groups. The system enforces a strict one-level nesting limit, preventing subcategories from creating their own subcategories to maintain a flat and browseable catalog structure.

Unique name constraints ensure clarity within each hierarchy level, requiring siblings to have distinct names. Soft deletion capabilities via the `deleted_at` field allow administrators to remove categories for cleanup without destructive impacts on historical order data and product listings.
IEcommercePlatformCategory.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from `ecommerce_platform_categories` table, including all columns and self-referential relations (`parentCategory`, `childrenCategories`). The `products` relation and raw `parent_ecommerce_platform_category_id` column are excluded as products belong to separate dedicated endpoints and the FK column is exposed via the `parentCategory` relation object.

sku_code.description:
Optional filter to narrow variant snapshot results by SKU code.

Accepts exact SKU code matching or partial substring matching against historical variant identifiers. Useful for auditing specific variant configurations across time. Leave empty or omit to retrieve all SKU codes in the result set.
sku_code.x-autobe-specification:
Server-side filter against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.sku_code column. Supports exact match when full SKU code provided, or partial substring match when abbreviated text supplied. No type transformation required.

Examples: 'SKU-12345' (exact match), 'SKU-123' (partial match matching any code containing this substring)

price.description:
Optional filter to narrow variant snapshot results by exact price value.

Requires exact price match (double-precision floating-point) against the price recorded at snapshot time. Useful for auditing pricing history or identifying snapshots at specific price points. Omit this filter to retrieve snapshots at all price levels.
price.x-autobe-specification:
Server-side filter against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.price column. Exact double-precision floating-point match — snapshots must have price exactly equal to the provided value. Accepts null check by omitting filter.

No rounding or approximate matching applied. Example: filtering price=29.99 returns only snapshots recorded at precisely $29.99.

stock_quantity.description:
Optional filter to narrow variant snapshot results by exact stock quantity.

Requires precise integer match against inventory quantity recorded at snapshot time. Useful for auditing stockout events (quantity=0) or specific inventory thresholds. Omit this filter to retrieve snapshots across all stock quantity levels.
stock_quantity.x-autobe-specification:
Server-side filter against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.stock_quantity column. Exact integer match — returned snapshots must have stock_quantity exactly equal to the specified integer value.

No range matching — use pagination or multiple requests for range-based queries. Example: filtering stock_quantity=0 returns only snapshots where variant was out of stock.

created_at_from.description:
Optional filter specifying the start boundary for snapshot creation date range.

Accepts RFC 3339 date-time string. Inclusive — snapshots created at exactly this timestamp are included. Combine with created_at_to to filter snapshots within a specific time window. Omit to include all snapshots regardless of creation date.
created_at_from.x-autobe-specification:
Server-side range filter boundary against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.created_at column. Inclusive lower bound — snapshots created_at timestamps greater than or equal to this value are included.

Format: RFC 3339 date-time string (ISO 8601). Combined with created_at_to for range filtering; used alone returns snapshots from this timestamp onward. Example: '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z' retrieves all snapshots created on or after January 15, 2024.

created_at_to.description:
Optional filter specifying the end boundary for snapshot creation date range.

Accepts RFC 3339 date-time string. Inclusive — snapshots created at exactly this timestamp are included. Combine with created_at_from to filter snapshots within a specific time window. Omit to include all snapshots regardless of creation date.
created_at_to.x-autobe-specification:
Server-side range filter boundary against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.created_at column. Inclusive upper bound — snapshots created_at timestamps less than or equal to this value are included.

Format: RFC 3339 date-time string (ISO 8601). Combined with created_at_from for range filtering; used alone returns snapshots up to and including this timestamp. Example: '2024-06-30T23:59:59Z' retrieves all snapshots through end of June 2024.

page.description:
Pagination page number for navigating through paginated snapshot result sets.

1-indexed integer (minimum 1). Determines which subset of filtered results to retrieve. Combined with limit parameter to control result set size. Check pagination metadata in response to determine valid page range and total pages available.
page.x-autobe-specification:
Pagination control parameter. 1-indexed integer specifying which page of results to return. Minimum value is 1 (first page). No maximum limit enforced server-side — clients should validate page bounds using total pages from pagination response.

Combined with limit parameter to calculate result offset: offset = (page - 1) * limit. Example: page=2 with limit=25 returns records 26-50.

limit.description:
Maximum number of variant snapshot records to return per page.

Integer between 1 and 100 (inclusive). Controls pagination page size. Higher values reduce number of API calls needed but increase response payload size. Default behavior if omitted follows server-side defaults. Check total records and total pages in response pagination metadata for complete result set bounds.
limit.x-autobe-specification:
Pagination control parameter specifying maximum number of snapshot records to return per page. Integer value between 1 and 100 (inclusive).

Controls result set size for each page request. Combined with page parameter. Server caps at 100; if client requests limit > 100, server returns exactly 100 records. Final page may contain fewer records than limit when total results don't evenly divide by limit value.

Example: limit=20 returns up to 20 snapshot records per page.

IEcommercePlatformSnapshotVariant.IReque.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for querying product variant snapshot history through paginated list endpoints.

This request DTO enables filtering the immutable audit trail of product variant states by SKU code, price, stock quantity, and creation date ranges, combined with pagination controls to navigate through large historical result sets. Used by sellers to browse snapshots of their own product variants and by administrators to audit any variant snapshot across the marketplace.
IEcommercePlatformSnapshotVariant.IReque.x-autobe-specification:
Query-time request DTO for product variant snapshot history at PATCH /ecommercePlatform/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/snapshots and PATCH /ecommercePlatform/admin/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/snapshots endpoints. No direct database table mapping — all properties are server-side query parameters and filters.

Server-side filter application:
- sku_code: Matches against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.sku_code column (exact or partial match)
- price: Exact match against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.price column
- stock_quantity: Exact match against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.stock_quantity column
- created_at_from through created_at_to: Inclusive date range filtering against ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variants.created_at column
- page (1-indexed, minimum 1) and limit (1-100): Pagination controls for result set navigation

Results returned as IPageIEcommercePlatformSnapshotVariant.ISummary. Path parameters productId and variantId scope queries to specific product-variant pairs; validators confirm variantId belongs to productId via ecommerce_platform_product_variants.ecommerce_platform_product_id FK relationship. Authorization enforces seller ownership (seller_profile_id) or administrator unrestricted access.

IEcommercePlatformSnapshot.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a snapshot record from the immutable audit trail, capturing the entity type that was modified and when the change occurred.

Snapshots are automatically generated for every modification to editable platform entities—products, product variants, seller profiles, order items, reviews, cancellation requests, and refund requests. This summary type provides lightweight entries for paginated list responses without loading detailed before-and-after state comparisons.

For detailed change comparison data by entity type, reference the specific snapshot detail types (e.g., IEcommercePlatformSnapshotProduct, IEcommercePlatformSnapshotVariant).

Used in paginated list responses for admin snapshot browsing at PATCH /ecommercePlatform/admin/snapshots and seller snapshot browsing endpoints.

Request body for creating a new shipment by bundling order items and providing carrier tracking information.

Sellers use this payload to dispatch physical packages containing one or more paid order items. IEcommercePlatformOrder.description:
Complete order record containing purchase transaction details, line items, and delivery information.

Orders are never deleted and preserved indefinitely for legal compliance, seller financial records, and customer purchase history. The order status reflects the collective lifecycle state of all contained order items.

Includes the customer profile that placed the order, the immutable shipping address captured at checkout, and all order line items with their product variant details, quantities, unit prices, and individual fulfillment statuses.

This schema provides essential context for browsing cancellation requests, including the request status, customer reason for cancellation, and the seller's response reason if rejected. The type includes references to the associated order item and customer who submitted the request, enabling list views to show sufficient information for administrative review and customer request tracking.

The status field indicates whether the request is pending seller review, approved by the seller, or rejected. Seller rejection reasons are included only when the seller denies the cancellation request.

Excluded: updated_at (not essential for list summaries), snapshots (HAS-MANY relation accessed via separate endpoint).

IEcommercePlatformProduct.ISummary.description:
Summarizes a product for paginated product listings and storefront search results.

Includes essential product identity fields: unique identifier, name, description, base price, and creation timestamp. IEcommercePlatformRefundRequest.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating refund request records.

Use this payload to query refund requests across the platform. Supports filtering by request status (pending, approved, or rejected), specific seller profiles, creation date ranges, response date ranges, and full-text search on refund reasons. Results are returned in pages of configurable size, sorted by creation date in descending order by default.

Access control is enforced automatically: sellers will only see refund requests assigned to their own profile, while administrators can view all requests platform-wide.

Pagination: `page` (default 1, 1-indexed), `limit` (default 20, max 100). Sort order: `created_at` descending by default. Set to 'approved' to accept the refund, which transitions the order item to 'refunded' status and restores product inventory stock. Must be an integer between 1 (lowest) and 5 (highest), inclusive. Omitting this field preserves the review's current rating.

This optional field supports three behaviors:
- Set to a string value: replaces the existing comment with new text content
- Set to null: removes any existing written comment while preserving the star rating
- Omitted from request: preserves the current text content unchanged

This flexibility enables rating-only reviews to later gain comments, or existing comments to be modified or removed independently of the star rating.

IEcommercePlatformReview.IUpdate.description:
Request body for partially updating a product review.

Customers can modify either the star rating, the written comment, both, or neither in a single request. Each field is optional following the partial update pattern.

The star rating must be between 1 and 5 inclusive if provided. The text content can be set to a new string value, set to null to remove any existing comment, or omitted to preserve the current content.

Reviews can only be edited by their original author, validated through JWT authentication. The review identified by the path parameter reviewId must exist and not be previously deleted.

Per IUpdate pattern, only fields that customers can modify are included - all other database properties are excluded. The ecommerce_platform_customer_id is resolved from JWT authentication identifying the review owner. The ecommerce_platform_product_id and ecommerce_platform_order_id are immutable structural FKs - reviews cannot change which product they review or which order context they belong to. Timestamps are server-managed. Before any update, the service automatically creates a snapshot record for audit trail purposes. Both fields are optional - omitting a field preserves its current value.

Shipments bundle order items from the same seller into a single delivery package with carrier name, tracking number, and shipping timeline. Upon shipment creation, all included order items transition to shipped status. IEcommercePlatformRefundRequest.description:
Complete refund request entity representing the lifecycle of a customer-initiated refund claim for a delivered order item.

Refund requests follow a three-state workflow: customers submit requests with a pending status and textual justification, then sellers review and either approve or reject the request. The seller is automatically identified through the product ownership chain (order item → product variant → product → seller profile). Upon approval, the associated order item transitions to refunded status and inventory stock is restored. Upon rejection, the order item remains in delivered status.

This entity links to the affected order item for purchase context and the assigned seller profile for ownership tracking. Timestamps capture both submission time and seller response time for audit purposes.

FK columns transformed to relation objects: order_item_id scalar → orderItem as $ref to IEcommercePlatformOrderItem.ISummary via LEFT JOIN; seller_profile_id scalar → sellerProfile as $ref to IEcommercePlatformSellerProfile.ISummary via LEFT JOIN. Business rules: status enum values are 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. responded_at is nullable (null while pending, populated when seller responds). One refund request per order_item enforced by unique constraint. refundRequestSnapshots relation excluded — aggregated snapshots accessed via separate snapshot endpoint.

Validates that the address exists, is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL), and belongs to the authenticated customer via ecommerce_platform_customer_profiles lookup. If validation fails, the entire checkout is rejected.

Checkout request specifying the delivery destination for the customer's shopping cart.

This request body is submitted when a customer initiates checkout. It captures the shipping address UUID that will be immutably associated with the newly created order. The customer's identity is resolved from the active session, and all order metadata including order number, line items, and fulfillment status are generated automatically by the backend.

During checkout, extracts shipping_address_id and populates ecommerce_platform_orders.ecommerce_platform_shipping_address_id. The customer's profile ID is resolved from the JWT session via ecommerce_platform_customer_profiles JOIN. Order number, aggregate status ('paid'), and timestamps are auto-generated server-side during the checkout transaction. Cart items are transformed into order items and soft-deleted from the cart within the same transaction.

IEcommercePlatformProduct.ISearch.description:
Search criteria for browsing products with optional filters for category, price range, and stock availability.

Use this request body to filter and paginate product listings in the storefront. Supports category-based filtering with subcategory expansion, price range queries, stock availability filtering, and configurable sort orders. All parameters are optional; omitting filters returns the complete catalog of active products. Uses cursor-based pagination for efficient large dataset navigation.

IEcommercePlatformProduct.ISearch.x-autobe-specification:
Search request DTO for PATCH /ecommercePlatform/customer/search endpoint. Queries ecommerce_platform_products with the following logic:

1. Only active products (deleted_at IS NULL) are returned
2. Products belonging to banned sellers are excluded (JOIN seller_profiles, filter is_banned = false)
3. categoryId: LEFT JOIN ecommerce_platform_categories, filter by category ID including all subcategories (one level nesting)
4. minPrice/maxPrice: filter on base_price column (>= minPrice, <= maxPrice)
5. inStockOnly: JOIN product_variants and inventory_records, calculate current stock, filter products with stock > 0
6. sortBy: ORDER BY created_at DESC (newest), base_price ASC (priceAsc), or base_price DESC (priceDesc). Default: newest
7. cursor + limit: Cursor-based pagination implementation

All properties are optional - omitting filters returns all active, non-banned products.

currentStock.description:
Computational current stock quantity.

Represents calculated result of summing all inventory_records.quantity_delta entries. Includes restocking (+ positive), orders (- negative), cancellations (+ positive), and refunds (+positive) events. When no records exist for a variant, defaults to 0 units.
currentStock.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregate formula:

COALESCE(SUM(inventory_records.quantity_delta), 0).

Joined on: inventory_records.ecommerce_platform_product_variant_id = variant.id.

Business rules:
- Variants with no inventory entries compute to 0 units.
- Negative values permitted in calculation.
- REPEATABLE READ transactions for consistent aggregate results.

availabilityStatus.description:
The stock availability status.

Computed enum indicating stock availability from currentStock:
- 'in_stock' if currentStock > 0: Available for purchase.
- 'out_of_stock' if currentStock <= 0: Not available for purchase.

Derived from the aggregate currentStock value across inventory events.
availabilityStatus.x-autobe-specification:
Computed enum formula:

IF currentStock > 0 THEN 'in_stock' ELSE 'out_of_stock'.

Derived from the sum of inventory_records.quantity_delta values joined on: inventory_records.ecommerce_platform_product_variant_id = variant.id.

IEcommercePlatformStockAnalytic.ISummary.description:
Current stock levels for product variants, aggregating data from the product inventory system.

Provides the real-time availability status, computed from the immutable inventory ledger. Includes variant details, product information, seller shop identification, and category assignment. The current stock quantity is calculated from all inventory events (restocking, order fulfillment, cancellations, refunds). Only active (non-deleted) variants and products are included.

This type does not map to a single database table but represents cross-table joins with aggregation from:

- ecommerce_platform_product_variants
- ecommerce_platform_products
- ecommerce_platform_seller_profiles
- ecommerce_platform_categories
- ecommerce_platform_inventory_records
IEcommercePlatformStockAnalytic.ISummary.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from multiple tables with no single database source.

Source tables and JOINs:
- ecommerce_platform_product_variants (id, sku_code, price)
- ecommerce_platform_products (id, name, base_price)
- ecommerce_platform_seller_profiles (id, shop_name)
- ecommerce_platform_categories (id, name)
- ecommerce_platform_inventory_records (ecommerce_platform_product_variant_id, quantity_delta)

Aggregation formulas:
- currentStock = COALESCE(SUM(inventory_records.quantity_delta), 0)
- availabilityStatus = IF currentStock > 0 THEN 'in_stock' ELSE 'out_of_stock'

Business rules:
- Deleted variants and products excluded (WHERE variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND product.deleted_at IS NULL)
- Variants with no inventory records: currentStock = 0, availabilityStatus = 'out_of_stock'
- Negative stock values permitted in calculation
- Use REPEATABLE READ isolation for consistent aggregates

Field mapping:
- variantId = product_variants.id
- skuCode = product_variants.sku_code.
- variantPrice = product_variants.price (nullable)
- productId = products.id
- productName = products.name
- productBasePrice = products.base_price
- sellerProfileId = seller_profiles.id
- shopName = seller_profiles.shop_name
- categoryId = categories.id
- categoryName = categories.name
- currentStock = computed aggregate
- availabilityStatus = computed enum

IEcommercePlatformStockAnalytic.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating product variant stock analytics results.

This query object enables sellers and administrators to browse inventory levels across product variants with flexible filtering options. All fields are optional — omitting all filters returns stock data for all active variants platform-wide.

Filtering is supported by seller profile, category, product, SKU code (partial match), stock availability status, and numeric stock level ranges. Results can be sorted by stock quantity, SKU code, product name, shop name, or creation date in ascending or descending order.

Pagination uses cursor-based navigation for efficient large-dataset browsing, with an alternative offset-based page/limit mode available.
IEcommercePlatformStockAnalytic.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query filter DTO for the stock analytics aggregation endpoint that computes current stock levels across all product variants.

Data sources and JOIN chain:
- ecommerce_platform_product_variants (primary aggregation source)
- ecommerce_platform_inventory_records (stock delta source)
- ecommerce_platform_products (product details)
- ecommerce_platform_seller_profiles (seller/shop details)
- ecommerce_platform_categories (category details)

Aggregation logic:
1. JOIN product_variants to inventory_records on variant.id = record.ecommerce_platform_product_variant_id
2. JOIN products on variant.ecommerce_platform_product_id = product.id
3. JOIN seller_profiles on product.ecommerce_platform_seller_profile_id = seller_profile.id
4. JOIN categories on product.ecommerce_platform_category_id = category.id
5. Filter: variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND product.deleted_at IS NULL
6. Aggregate: current_stock = COALESCE(SUM(quantity_delta), 0) per variant
7. Compute: availability_status = 'in_stock' IF current_stock > 0 ELSE 'out_of_stock'

Filter application:
- seller_profile_id: WHERE seller_profile.id = value
- category_id: WHERE category.id = value
- product_id: WHERE product.id = value
- sku_code: WHERE sku_code LIKE value (partial match)
- availability_status: WHERE availability_status = value
- min_stock_level: WHERE current_stock >= value
- max_stock_level: WHERE current_stock <= value

Sorting:
- sort_by: ORDER BY field (current_stock, sku_code, product_name, shop_name, created_at)
- sort_order: ASC or DESC, default DESC
- Default sort: created_at DESC

Pagination:
- Cursor-based: page_size and cursor
- Offset-based: page and limit (legacy alternative)
- Defaults: page_size=20, page=1, limit=100

Transaction isolation: REPEATABLE READ for consistent aggregates during concurrent writes.

Negative stock values are permitted in calculation per business rules.

Returns IEcommercePlatformSnapshotVariant.ISummary containing sku_code, price, stock_quantity captured at snapshot time, plus normalized option key-value pairs joined from ecommerce_platform_snapshot_variant_options WHERE the snapshot_variant_id matches. This property exposes the HAS-ONE variantSnapshot relation as a nested $ref object rather than scalar FK ID per Response DTO FK-to-$ref transformation rules.

product_variant.description:

IEcommercePlatformSnapshot.IInvert.description:
A snapshot record capturing a product variant at a specific point in time.

This schema is returned by the admin and seller GET endpoints for retrieving a single product variant snapshot by its unique identifier. It combines the immutable polymorphic snapshot header (id, entity_type, created_at) with the variant-specific snapshot data encapsulated as a reference to {@link IEcommercePlatformSnapshotVariant.ISummary}, which includes SKU code, price, stock quantity, and normalized option key-value pairs.

Additionally, it includes a reference to the current product variant summary ({@link IEcommercePlatformProductVariant.ISummary}) for catalog context, allowing comparison of the historical snapshot against the variant's present configuration.

The entity_type is always 'product_variant' for responses from variant snapshot endpoints.
IEcommercePlatformSnapshot.IInvert.x-autobe-specification: Aggregate polymorphic snapshot header (ecommerce_platform_snapshots) with id, entity_type, and created_at. The entity_type is always 'product_variant' for this snapshot type.

IEcommercePlatformOrder.IFulfillmentSumm.description:

The `orderNumber` uniquely identifies the purchase transaction, while `status` reflects the overall fulfillment state (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, or partially_completed). IEcommercePlatformCustomerPasswordReset..description:

Both fields are required. The current password is verified against stored credentials before the new password is applied. Upon successful change, all active sessions are invalidated.
IEcommercePlatformCustomerPasswordReset..x-autobe-specification: Request body for password change operation. Fields currentPassword and newPassword are plain text passwords. Backend must bcrypt-compare currentPassword against stored password_hash in the appropriate table (ecommerce_platform_customers, ecommerce_platform_sellers, or ecommerce_platform_admins based on session actor type). After successful change, all existing sessions for the user are invalidated.

revokedCount.description:
The total number of active sessions that were successfully revoked for the authenticated user.

This value is always non-negative and will be zero if no active sessions were found at the time of revocation. Represents the count of sessions terminated across all devices.
revokedCount.x-autobe-specification:
Computed integer value representing the number of active sessions revoked. Derived from affected row counts during the session revocation transaction:
- customer: COUNT from UPDATE SET deleted_at ON ecommerce_platform_customer_sessions
- seller: COUNT from DELETE ON ecommerce_platform_seller_sessions
- admin: COUNT from DELETE ON ecommerce_platform_admin_sessions

Always non-negative (minimum 0). Returns 0 when no active sessions exist.

IEcommercePlatformActiveSessionRevocatio.description:
Confirmation response for bulk session revocation operations.

Returns the total count of active sessions that were successfully terminated for the authenticated user. This response confirms successful execution of the revoke-all operation regardless of whether any sessions were actually found.
IEcommercePlatformActiveSessionRevocatio.x-autobe-specification:
Computed confirmation response DTO generated by the revoke-all session operation handler. This schema is not mapped to any database table — all properties are server-side computed values.

The `revokedCount` property is derived by counting the number of affected rows during session revocation. The revocation logic differs by actor type:
- For customer: COUNT of rows from soft-delete UPDATE on ecommerce_platform_customer_sessions
- For seller: COUNT of rows from DELETE on ecommerce_platform_seller_sessions
- For admin: COUNT of rows from DELETE on ecommerce_platform_admin_sessions

The count reflects only active (non-expired) sessions at the time of revocation. Zero is returned if no active sessions exist.

IEcommercePlatformAdminAuditLog.description:
Administrative audit log record capturing a governance action performed by a platform administrator.

This immutable, append-only record serves as the definitive source for compliance tracking, dispute resolution, and platform intervention history. Each log entry identifies the performing administrator, the affected entity via polymorphic targeting (targetType and targetId), the specific governance action executed (action), an optional justification reason, and the exact timestamp of the action (createdAt).

Audit log records are permanent and cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring full accountability for all platform interventions including account management, seller approvals, category operations, product oversight, and order interventions.

ecommerce_platform_product_variant_id.description:
The UUID of the product variant being purchased.

References the specific SKU configuration (e.g., color: Red, size: Large) from the product catalog. This foreign key identifies exactly which variant the customer wants to purchase.

Required to validate stock availability, calculate pricing, and deduct inventory during order placement. Creates a unique constraint with the parent order to prevent duplicate variants in the same order.

Unique constraint exists with ecommerce_platform_order_id to prevent duplicate variants in same order.

quantity.description:

Combined with the per-unit price, this determines the total cost for this line item.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_platform_order_items.quantity (Int, minimum 1). Represents the number of units of the specific product variant ordered by the customer. Validated against available stock at purchase time. Serves as the basis for stock deduction via inventory records.

price.description:
The per-unit price for this product variant at the time of purchase.

A floating-point number representing the agreed-upon price at checkout. This becomes an immutable historical financial record.

Combined with quantity, this determines the total cost for this line item. Essential for order total calculation, revenue tracking, and refund calculations.
price.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_platform_order_items.price (Float/DoublePrecision, minimum 0). Captures the per-unit price at the exact moment of purchase as an immutable historical financial record. Remains unchanged even if the product variant's current price is later modified. Captured from cart calculation before order creation.

IEcommercePlatformOrderItem.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a specific order line item within an order.

Contains the product variant reference, purchase quantity, and per-unit price for an individual line item. Submit this as part of the items array in an order creation request to specify which product variants, in what quantities, and at what prices the customer is purchasing.

The price field captures the agreed-upon value between customer and seller at the moment of purchase and becomes an immutable historical financial record, remaining unchanged even if the product variant's current price is later modified.

Maps: ecommerce_platform_product_variant_id (FK to product variant, required for stock deduction and variant identification), quantity (Int, minimum 1, units ordered), price (Float, minimum 0, immutable per-unit price at purchase time). Excluded: id (UUID auto-generated), ecommerce_platform_order_id (parent FK set during nested creation from parent order), status (auto-set to 'paid'), created_at/updated_at (auto-generated timestamps), order (parent relation resolved from nested transaction), productVariant (FK relation exposed as scalar in Request DTO), shipmentItem/cancellationRequests/refundRequest/itemSnapshots (has relations created later by system).

These are pending requests from customers to cancel order items, requiring the seller to approve or reject.
totalPendingCancellationRequests.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests WHERE status = 'pending' AND the request's order_item references a product variant owned by the authenticated seller.

totalPendingRefundRequests.description:
The number of customer refund requests awaiting seller decision.

These are pending refund claims for delivered items, requiring the seller to review and approve or reject.
totalPendingRefundRequests.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_platform_refund_requests WHERE status = 'pending' AND the request's order_item references a product variant owned by the authenticated seller.

IEcommercePlatformSellerDashboard.description:
Aggregated seller dashboard overview containing account status, storefront details, and business metrics.

This view consolidates the authenticated seller's operational snapshot in a single response, including their platform approval status and rejection details, active shop profile information, and key performance metrics such as product counts, order volumes, and pending customer requests.
IEcommercePlatformSellerDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregated dashboard view for the authenticated seller, combining data from two tables:

1. **ecommerce_platform_sellers** (WHERE id = authenticated seller id from JWT):
   - approval_status → approvalStatus
   - rejection_reason → rejectionReason (nullable)

2. **ecommerce_platform_seller_profiles** (WHERE seller_id = authenticated seller id):
   - shop_name → shopName
   - shop_description → shopDescription
   - logo_image_uri → logoImageUri

3. **Computed aggregations**:
   - totalProducts: COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_platform_products WHERE seller_profile_id = seller.sellerProfile.id AND deleted_at IS NULL
   - totalOrderItems: COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_platform_order_items oi JOIN ecommerce_platform_product_variants pv ON oi.product_variant_id = pv.id JOIN ecommerce_platform_products p ON pv.product_id = p.id WHERE p.seller_profile_id = seller.sellerProfile.id
   - totalPendingCancellationRequests: COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_platform_cancellation_requests cr JOIN ecommerce_platform_order_items oi ON cr.order_item_id = oi.id WHERE oi.product_variant_id IN (variants owned by seller) AND cr.status = 'pending'
   - totalPendingRefundRequests: COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_platform_refund_requests rr JOIN ecommerce_platform_order_items oi ON rr.order_item_id = oi.id WHERE oi.product_variant_id IN (variants owned by seller) AND rr.status = 'pending'

IEcommercePlatformReview.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for listing product reviews across the ecommerce platform.

Used by both authenticated customers and guests to browse customer feedback on products. Supports text search on review content, filtering by specific product, customer, or order context, rating range constraints (1-5 scale), and date range filters on creation or modification timestamps. All fields are optional to enable flexible browsing, and results are sorted newest-first by default following business rules for display requirements.
IEcommercePlatformReview.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: All properties optional following IRequest pattern. Base query: SELECT from ecommerce_platform_reviews WHERE deleted_at IS NULL excluding soft-deleted reviews. Text search on text_content column using case-insensitive LIKE match. Exact match filters on ecommerce_platform_product_id, ecommerce_platform_customer_id, and ecommerce_platform_order_id. Rating range: minRating >= rating >= maxRating with integer constraint 1-5. Date range filters on created_at and updated_at columns using >= and <= operators. Pagination via page (1-indexed, defaults to 1) and limit (1-100, defaults to 20). Default ORDER BY created_at DESC for newest-first sorting.

id.description:

Integer value between 1 and 5 representing the rating that existed before the customer edited their review. Null when this snapshot captures the initial creation of a review, as no previous rating existed. Always present for edit snapshots.

Integer value between 1 and 5 representing the current rating of the review following the modification. Always present and non-null, reflecting the latest state whether this is a creation or edit snapshot. This value contributes to the product's average rating calculation.
new_rating.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_platform_snapshot_reviews.new_rating. Non-nullable integer 1-5. Always contains the current rating state after the modification event.

new_content.description:
The text content after the modification; null for star-only reviews.

The written comment representing the current state of the review following the modification. Nullable — null when the review contains only a star rating without text content. Always present and reflects the latest content state.
new_content.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_platform_snapshot_reviews.new_content. Nullable string. Contains the current text content of the review after the modification, or null if the review is star-only.

created_at.description:

IEcommercePlatformSnapshotReview.ISummar.description:
Summary of an immutable review snapshot record capturing the before and after state of a review modification.

Each snapshot preserves the star rating and text content as they existed before and after a customer edits their review. For newly created reviews, the previous state fields (previous_rating, previous_content) are null. Snapshots serve as an immutable audit trail for dispute resolution and platform oversight.

Snapshots are sorted newest first by default in list queries and cannot be modified or deleted by any user, including administrators.
IEcommercePlatformSnapshotReview.ISummar.x-autobe-specification: Source: ecommerce_platform_snapshot_reviews LEFT JOIN ecommerce_platform_snapshots ON snapshot_reviews.ecommerce_platform_snapshot_id = snapshots.id WHERE entity_type='review'. Direct field mappings: id from snapshot_reviews.id (UUID), previous_rating from snapshot_reviews.previous_rating (nullable Int 1-5, null for creation snapshots), previous_content from snapshot_reviews.previous_content (nullable String), new_rating from snapshot_reviews.new_rating (Int 1-5 always present), new_content from snapshot_reviews.new_content (nullable String). BELONGS-TO relation: review via LEFT JOIN ecommerce_platform_reviews on ecommerce_platform_review_id → $ref IEcommercePlatformReview.ISummary per FK transformation rules. Timestamp: created_at from ecommerce_platform_snapshots.created_at via the snapshot join. Excluded: updated_at (snapshots immutable), ecommerce_platform_snapshot_id (internal plumbing FK), ecommerce_platform_review_id (scalar FK transformed to review object), snapshot (internal polymorphic header relation).

IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing administrator promotion requests. Filter requests by actor type (customer or seller), lifecycle status (pending, approved, or rejected), review completion state, specific reviewer administrator, and submission or review date ranges. Supports text search across justification and rejection reason fields.

Pagination uses page numbers with configurable page size (default 20, maximum 100). Sort results by any filterable field in ascending or descending order. Defaults to showing most recent requests first.
IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameter DTO for filtering and paginating administrator promotion request listings.

All properties are optional. Filter properties map to WHERE clause conditions on ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests columns. Range parameters (created_at_from/to, reviewed_at_from/to) generate BETWEEN conditions. The reviewed boolean generates reviewed_at IS NOT NULL / IS NULL. The search parameter generates ILIKE conditions on reason and rejection_reason columns. Pagination uses page/limit for offset-based navigation. Sort directive follows field-direction format (e.g., created_at-desc, status-asc). Default sort is created_at DESC.

reviewed_by_admin_id maps directly to the DB column for exact UUID matching.

Used by PATCH endpoints on /admin/administrator-promotion-requests, /customer/administrator-promotion-requests, and /seller/administrator-promotion-requests.

IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.description:
Request payload for super administrators to approve or reject pending administrator promotion requests.

The status field transitions from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected'. When rejected, the rejectionReason field explains the decision basis. If approved, rejectionReason must not be provided.

Excluded:
- id: auto-generated primary key
- actor_type: immutable discriminator
- reason: requester's justification (immutable)
- reviewed_by_admin_id: extracted from authentication context
- reviewed_at: auto-populated timestamp
- created_at/updated_at: system-managed
IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.x-autobe-specification:
Maps to ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests. Updates status column from pending to approved or rejected. rejection_reason populated only when status='rejected'.

Business rules:
- status='approved' or 'rejected' (required)
- rejection_reason required when status='rejected', null when status='approved'
- reviewed_by_admin_id auto-populated from JWT auth context
- reviewed_at auto-populated with current timestamp on status change
- actor_type and reason are immutable
- id is auto-generated

Validations:
- status must be 'approved' or 'rejected', cannot be 'pending'
- rejection_reason must be non-null and non-empty when status='rejected'
- rejection_reason must be null when status='approved'
- Reject 409 if status already 'approved' or 'rejected'
- Reject 400 if status='rejected' and rejection_reason is null/empty
- Reject 422 if status='approved' and rejection_reason is provided

Immutable fields: actor_type, reason
Excluded from request: id (auto-generated), reviewed_by_admin_id (JWT), reviewed_at (auto-populated), created_at/updated_at (system-managed)

IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.description:
Summary of an administrator promotion request for the paginated list view.

Contains identification, lifecycle, and review context fields:

- id: Primary key identifier for the promotion request.
- actor_type: Discriminator of the request type, either customer requesting admin role or seller requesting admin role.
- status: Current lifecycle status of the promotion request.
- reason: Written justification provided by the requester explaining why they should be granted administrator privileges.
- rejection_reason: Explanation provided by the reviewing super administrator when the request was rejected.
- reviewed_at: Timestamp when the super administrator completed their review and changed the status from pending to approved or rejected.
- reviewedByAdmin: The super administrator who reviewed and responded to this promotion request.
IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.x-autobe-specification: Maps to ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests columns: id, actor_type, status, reason, rejection_reason, reviewed_at, reviewed_by_admin_id (as reviewedByAdmin relation). Relations: BELONGS-TO reviewedByAdmin via reviewed_by_admin_id FK, represented as nullable $ref to IEcommercePlatformAdmin.ISummary. No compositions present. No aggregations. System timestamps excluded.

items.description:
Active shopping cart line items for the authenticated customer.

Each element represents a customer's purchase intent for a specific product variant at a desired quantity. Items include full detail references to the owning customer, the product variant, quantity, and lifecycle timestamps. Product and variant information are embedded through relationship joins.

Computed at query time: per-item subtotal (quantity multiplied by variant-specific price or product base price fallback), current stock availability (summed from the immutable inventory ledger), and unavailability flags for items with zero stock or deleted products/variants. The array is empty when the customer has no active cart items.
items.x-autobe-specification: Query ecommerce_platform_shopping_cart_items WHERE ecommerce_platform_customer_id = authenticated customer ID AND deleted_at IS NULL. Join with ecommerce_platform_product_variants ON product_variant_id and ecommerce_platform_products ON product_id. Return array of IEcommercePlatformShoppingCartItem objects. Compute per-item subtotal = quantity * COALESCE(product_variant.price, product.base_price). Compute stock availability per item by SUM(inventory_records.quantity_delta) per variant. Flag items as unavailable when stock < 1 OR product.deleted_at IS NOT NULL OR product_variant.deleted_at IS NULL. Filter output to exclude soft-deleted cart items.

totalPrice.description:
Total cart price for checkout pricing calculations.

Represents the computed total monetary value summing all line-item subtotals in the authenticated customer's shopping cart. Each item subtotal is computed individually as quantity multiplied by the applicable unit price (variant-specific price when present, otherwise the product's base price). The total is the summation of all item subtotals.

This aggregation updates in real-time as items are added, removed, or have their quantities modified. Returns 0 when the shopping cart contains no items.
totalPrice.x-autobe-specification: Compute SUM per shopping cart item: quantity * COALESCE(ecommerce_platform_product_variants.price, ecommerce_platform_products.base_price) for items WHERE ecommerce_platform_customer_id = authenticated customer ID AND deleted_at IS NULL. Sum all computed item subtotals to produce totalPrice. Join ecommerce_platform_shopping_cart_items with ecommerce_platform_product_variants ON product_variant_id and ecommerce_platform_products ON product_id. Filter: WHERE ecommerce_platform_shopping_cart_items.deleted_at IS NULL AND product_variant.deleted_at IS NULL. Return 0 when no items exist in the cart for the authenticated customer.

IEcommercePlatformShoppingCartItem.IStat.description:
Shopping cart status for the authenticated customer.

Returns the complete current state of the customer's shopping cart, including all active line items with their product and variant details, computed subtotals, stock availability status, unavailability warnings, and the total cart price for checkout calculations. This is an aggregated view computed at query time by joining shopping cart items with product variant and product data.

Returns an empty items array and a totalPrice of 0 when the customer has no active cart items. Only non-deleted cart items are included; soft-deleted items are automatically filtered out from the result.
IEcommercePlatformShoppingCartItem.IStat.x-autobe-specification: Aggregation DTO returning the authenticated customer's shopping cart status. Data source: ecommerce_platform_shopping_cart_items JOIN ecommerce_platform_product_variants ON product_variant_id JOIN ecommerce_platform_products ON product_id. Scoped to authenticated customer. Computation: per-item subtotal = quantity * COALESCE(variant.price, product.base_price). Stock availability check: SUM(inventory_records.quantity_delta) per variant. Unavailability flag: stock < 1 OR product.deleted_at IS NOT NULL OR product_variant.deleted_at IS NOT NULL. totalPrice = SUM of all item subtotals. Returns empty array and 0 for empty carts.

IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.description:
Request body for submitting an administrator promotion application.

Provide your account type via actorType and explain your justification via reason. Upon submission, the request enters pending status and awaits review by a super administrator.

The actor type must correspond to your authenticated account role. Customers submit from the customer endpoint with 'customer', sellers submit from the seller endpoint with 'seller'. Backend validation ensures the provided actor type matches the authenticated actor's type from the JWT token. All other fields such as status, review timestamps, and reviewer information are managed automatically by the platform.
IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.x-autobe-specification:
Maps to ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests table for creating new administrator promotion requests.

User-provided fields:
- actorType -> actor_type: String discriminator restricted to 'customer' or 'seller'. Backend validates it matches the authenticated actor's type from the JWT token.
- reason -> reason: Required string containing the applicant's written justification for seeking administrator privileges.

System-initialized fields (not in request body):
- id: Auto-generated UUID primary key.
- status: Defaults to 'pending' on creation.
- reviewed_by_admin_id: Set to null initially, populated when a super administrator reviews.
- rejection_reason: Set to null initially, populated only upon rejection.
- reviewed_at: Set to null initially, populated when status changes from pending.
- created_at, updated_at: Auto-managed by the database.

Polymorphic subtype handling:
- After creating the main record, the system creates a corresponding subtype record:
  - If actor_type is 'customer', inserts into ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_request_of_customers
  - If actor_type is 'seller', inserts into ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_request_of_sellers
- The authenticated user's customer ID or seller ID is linked via the subtype table. This association is resolved from the JWT, not provided in the request body.

Validation rules:
- actor_type must match the authenticated user's account type
- reason must be non-empty text
- Check for existing pending request from same user (duplicate prevention)

rejectionReason.description:
Explanation provided by the super administrator when the promotion request was rejected.

This field contains the reviewer's reasoning for declining the application. It is populated only when the status is "rejected" and remains null for "pending" or "approved" requests.
rejectionReason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests.rejection_reason. Nullable string populated only when status is "rejected". Provides the reviewing super administrator's explanation for the rejection decision. Remains null when status is "pending" or "approved".

reviewedByAdmin.description:
Super administrator who reviewed and made a decision on this promotion request.

This object contains summary details of the reviewing administrator. It is populated only after a super administrator processes the request (status becomes "approved" or "rejected") and remains null while the request is pending.

The summary includes the administrator's unique identifier, grade level, and ban status.
reviewedByAdmin.x-autobe-specification: Join via ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests.reviewed_by_admin_id FK to ecommerce_platform_admins.id. Returns IEcommercePlatformAdmin.ISummary. Nullable: null while the request is in pending status, populated after a super administrator approves or rejects the request. On delete cascade from the admin table.

reviewedAt.description:
Timestamp when the super administrator completed their review and changed the request status.

This ISO 8601 datetime field is populated only after the request transitions from "pending" to "approved" or "rejected". It enables tracking of review response times and provides audit compliance timestamps.

Remains null while the request is in pending status.
reviewedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests.reviewed_at. Nullable DateTime (Timestamptz). Populated with the current timestamp when a super administrator completes their review. Enables audit compliance by recording the exact moment the request was processed. Remains null while pending.

IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.description:
Full entity details of an administrator promotion request submitted by a customer or seller seeking platform administrator privileges.

This schema represents the complete lifecycle of a promotion request, including the applicant's account type, written justification, current lifecycle status, and review details. Status transitions are strictly one-way: pending transitions to approved or rejected. Once processed, the request becomes immutable.

The reviewedByAdmin and reviewedAt fields are populated only after a super administrator reviews the request. They remain null while the request is in pending status.
IEcommercePlatformAdministratorPromotion.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the ecommerce_platform_administrator_promotion_requests table. FK transformation: reviewed_by_admin_id is transformed to reviewedByAdmin as a $ref to IEcommercePlatformAdmin.ISummary object (nullable: null while the request is pending). All scalar columns are directly mapped with camelCase naming. Timestamps are system-managed NOT NULL fields. Polymorphic subtype relations (customerPromotionSubtype, sellerSubtype) are not exposed in this Read DTO as they are managed through separate subtype tables.

This validates the idempotent behavior ensuring returning visitors can seamlessly continue their session without creating duplicate guest records.

scenario.draft: Test the primary success path of customer authentication token refresh. A new customer account is registered via the join endpoint, which creates the customer identity in ecommerce_platform_customers and establishes an initial active session in ecommerce_platform_customer_sessions with a refresh_token_hash and expiration. The test then extracts the refresh token from the IAuthorized response and submits it to the refresh endpoint. Upon successful validation, the token rotation mechanism generates a new JWT access token and a new refresh token. The session record is updated with the new refresh_token_hash, extended expiration, and updated timestamp. The initial IAuthorized response includes the access token, refresh token, expired_at timestamp, and refreshable_until deadline. The customer then refreshes their authentication by submitting the refresh token to the refresh endpoint. The system validates the refresh_token_hash matches, the session is active (not soft-deleted), the expiration has not passed, and the linked customer account exists and is not banned. Upon success, a new JWT token pair is generated and returned, allowing the customer to maintain platform access for browsing products, managing cart, placing orders, and submitting reviews. This workflow ensures continuous authentication experience as the original access token nears expiration without requiring the customer to re-enter credentials.

scenario.draft:
This scenario evaluates the business logic governing product availability status and the toggle parameter `includeUnavailable`.
1. Ensure system holds products in these states:
  - State A: Products having active variants (quantity > 0).
  - State B: Products having active variants but ALL are zero stock (quantity == 0).
  - State C: Products having no active variants (all are deleted or no variants created).
2. Call PATCH /ecommercePlatform/products with `includeUnavailable` left as default (false).
3. Verify State A products are included, showing `isAvailable` = 'active' and `variantCount` > 0. 
4. Verify State B products are included, showing `isAvailable` = 'outOfStock' and `variantCount` > 0.
5. Verify State C products are excluded entirely due to missing active variants from the EXISTS subquery.
6. Call PATCH /ecommercePlatform/products with `includeUnavailable` = true.
7. Verify State C products are now included in results. Check that they are correctly labeled with `isAvailable` = 'unavailable' and `variantCount` = 0. 
8. Validate State A and State B items remain accurate (`active` and `outOfStock`).

- Business integrity is maintained - no orphaned data is accessible through the public API

scenario.draft:
A seller uploads multiple product images in a single operation by submitting an array of image URIs. The system validates product ownership by ensuring the product's ecommerce_platform_seller_profile_id matches the authenticated seller's profile. A snapshot entry in ecommerce_platform_snapshots records the product image modifications. The response returns all newly created product image records including their assigned UUID identifiers and display order positions as an array of IEcommercePlatformProductImage objects. Images are immediately visible on the product detail page after creation, with the image at the lowest order_index serving as the main thumbnail for product listings.

Validation points:
- Product ownership confirmed (ecommerce_platform_seller_profile_id matches authenticated seller)
- All URIs in the request array are processed successfully
- Each new image receives a unique UUID in the id field
- Order indices assigned sequentially starting from 1 if no existing images (e.g., 1, 2, 3 for three images)
- Database transaction ensures atomic creation (all images created or none)
- Snapshot entry created in ecommerce_platform_snapshots
- Response contains array of all created IEcommercePlatformProductImage records with id, uri, order_index, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at fields
- Images are immediately queryable via product detail view

functions.name: test_api_product_variant_snapshot_option_filter

scenario.draft:
Validate that sellers can retrieve immutable snapshot variant option records created when they modify their product variants.

Setup workflow:
1. Admin creates a product category (prerequisite for product creation)
2. Seller creates a product in that category
3. Seller creates a variant with options (e.g., attributeKey="color", attributeValue="Red" and attributeKey="size", attributeValue="Large")
4. Seller updates the variant to change an option value (e.g., changes "color" from "Red" to "Blue")
   - This modification automatically creates an immutable snapshot preserving the variant's previous state including all option key-value pairs

Target operation validation:
- Retrieve the snapshot variant option using productId, variantId, snapshotId (from the snapshot generated by the PUT update), and optionId for one of the options
- Verify the returned IEcommercePlatformSnapshotVariantOption contains:
  - `key` matching the attribute name (e.g., "color")
  - `value` matching the PRESERVED pre-update value (e.g., "Red" — the value BEFORE the modification, not the current live "Blue")
  - `snapshotVariant` reference with correct sku_code, price, and stock_quantity captured at snapshot time
  - `created_at` timestamp aligned with the snapshot generation

This validates snapshot immutability and the audit trail purpose: the captured option data reflects the historical state before modification, enabling dispute resolution and change tracking.

functions.name: test_api_product_variant_snapshot_option_retrieval

scenario.draft:
Validate that multiple sequential variant edits create independent snapshots, each preserving the distinct before-state at the time of that specific edit.

Setup workflow:
1. Admin creates a category, seller creates a product and variant with color="Red" and size="Large"
2. First edit: Seller updates variant, changing color from "Red" to "Green" → Snapshot A captures (color="Red", size="Large")
3. Second edit: Seller updates variant again, changing color from "Green" to "Blue" → Snapshot B captures (color="Green", size="Large")

Target operation validation:
- Retrieve the snapshot option from Snapshot B (created by the second edit)
- Verify the option value is "Green" — the state BEFORE the second edit, NOT "Red" (original) and NOT "Blue" (current live state)
- Verify snapshotVariant reference reflects the variant state at time of Snapshot B

This validates snapshot isolation: each snapshot independently captures its own pre-modification state, creating a complete audit timeline of all changes rather than just the original value.

Seller B joins and creates their product with variant. Customer joins, creates address, and places a multi-seller order containing items from both Seller A and Seller B. System must reject because order items from different sellers cannot be grouped into a single shipment per the same-seller grouping rule. The entire transaction should be aborted as the validation checks that all items belong to the authenticated seller.

scenario.draft:
Test the primary success path where a customer successfully submits a cancellation request for an order item in 'paid' status that has not yet been shipped.

Prerequisites chain: Admin registers and creates a category (required to classify the product). The seller registers and creates a product in that category and adds a variant that has stock. Execution: The authenticated customer submits a cancellation request by providing the target order item ID and a cancellation reason (e.g., 'Changed my mind').

Validation points:
- Verify HTTP 201 Created response status
- Confirm the response object is the full cancellation request record
- Verify id field is a valid UUID
- Verify orderItem reference matches the submitted target order item
- Verify customer reference matches the authenticated customer's identity
- Verify reason is exactly the submitted cancellation reason
- Verify status is 'pending' awaiting seller review
- Verify seller_response_reason is null on creation
- Verify created_at and updated_at fields are valid ISO 8601 timestamps
- Verify timestamps reflect the current creation time

- Confirm the rejection is due to an existing cancellation request already associated with this order item
- Verify no second cancellation request record is created
- This validates the database @@unique constraint on ecommerce_platform_order_item_id preventing duplicate requests

- Product reference remains in database but is excluded from query results

scenario.draft:
Verify that administrators can retrieve immutable snapshot review records that capture the before-and-after state when a customer edits their product review.

Setup workflow:

- Response returns complete immutable snapshot review record
- previousRating equals 3 (original rating before edit)
- previousContent equals the original review text
- newRating equals 5 (updated rating after edit)
- newContent equals the updated review text
- snapshot reference contains entity type 'review' and creation timestamp
- review reference contains product details, seller info, and customer info
- All fields are immutable and cannot be modified

IEcommercePlatformProductImage.ICreate is a collectable DTO that maps to ecommerce_platform_product_images table. The productId path parameter provides the foreign key reference to ecommerce_platform_products. The DTO collects image URI with auto-assigned order_index and timestamps.

IEcommercePlatformShoppingCartItem.ICreate is a collectable Create DTO. It maps to ecommerce_platform_shopping_cart_items table with product_variant_id and quantity fields in the request body. The customer foreign key (ecommerce_platform_customer_id) is resolved from the authenticated customer actor via JWT session, not from the DTO body. References: ecommerce_platform_customers from authorized actor.

Collectable. IEcommercePlatformInventoryRecord.ICreate maps to ecommerce_platform_inventory_records table. Collects quantity_delta and reason fields. The FK ecommerce_platform_product_variant_id comes from path parameter variantId, not from the DTO body.

Collectable Create DTO. Maps to ecommerce_platform_refund_requests table. No path parameters in endpoint. Customer ownership validated through order_item chain, not stored as FK in refund_requests table.

import { TypedBody, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller, Ip } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia from "typia";

import { IEcommercePlatformGuest } from "../../../../api/structures/IEcommercePlatformGuest";
import { postEcommercePlatformAuthGuestJoin } from "../../../../providers/postEcommercePlatformAuthGuestJoin";
import { postEcommercePlatformAuthGuestRefresh } from "../../../../providers/postEcommercePlatformAuthGuestRefresh";

@Controller("/ecommercePlatform/auth/guest")
export class EcommerceplatformAuthGuestController {
  /**
   * Join endpoint for guest registration without credentials.
   *
   * Registers a new guest account or retrieves existing guest session using device fingerprint. The device fingerprint uniquely identifies visitors based on browser and device characteristics including user agent, screen resolution, and timezone.
   *
   * Upon successful join, the system creates or retrieves a guest record in ecommerce_platform_guests and establishes an authenticated session in ecommerce_platform_guest_sessions.
   *
   * No email or password required - guests authenticate via device fingerprint only. This enables unauthenticated visitors to access registration and login pages before creating full accounts.
   *
   * Related operations: refresh for token renewal.
   *
   * @setHeader token.access Authorization
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Join request containing device fingerprint for guest identification.
   *
   *             The device_fingerprint uniquely identifies the visitor based on browser and device characteristics including user agent, screen resolution, timezone, installed plugins, and other device attributes.
   *
   *             Field: device_fingerprint (string, required) - Unique identifier derived from visitor's browser and device characteristics. Must be a valid identifier that distinguishes this visitor from others.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type join
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor guest
   * @x-autobe-specification POST /auth/guest/join
   *
   * Service Logic:
   * 1. Extract device fingerprint from request body
   * 2. Query ecommerce_platform_guests for existing active guest with matching device_fingerprint (deleted_at IS NULL)
   * 3. If exists: use existing guest record and create fresh session
   * 4. If not exists: create new record in ecommerce_platform_guests with:
   *    - device_fingerprint from request
   *    - created_at = current timestamp
   *    - updated_at = current timestamp
   *    - deleted_at = null
   * 5. Create new session in ecommerce_platform_guest_sessions:
   *    - ecommerce_platform_guest_id = guest id
   *    - ip = request IP
   *    - href = current page URL
   *    - referrer = referrer URL
   *    - created_at = current timestamp
   *    - expired_at = created_at + session duration (24h default)
   * 6. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens
   * 7. Return IAuthorized response with tokens
   *
   * Edge Cases:
   * - Duplicate fingerprint: Idempotent - return existing guest tokens
   * - Invalid fingerprint format: 400 Bad Request
   * - Guest soft-deleted: Create new guest record
   *
   * Error Handling:
   * - 400: Invalid device fingerprint format (empty, too short, non-UUID)
   * - 500: Database error during guest/session creation
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post("join")
  public async join(
    @Ip()
    ip: string,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IEcommercePlatformGuest.IJoin,
  ): Promise<IEcommercePlatformGuest.IAuthorized> {
    try {
      return await postEcommercePlatformAuthGuestJoin({
        ip,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Refresh endpoint for renewing guest authentication tokens.
   *
   * Renews JWT access and refresh tokens for active guest sessions. Validates the provided refresh token against the guest's current session state in ecommerce_platform_guest_sessions.
   *
   * The system checks that the guest account exists in ecommerce_platform_guests, is not soft-deleted, and has an active session in ecommerce_platform_guest_sessions with expired_at in the future.
   *
   * Returns new tokens enabling continued guest authentication for accessing registration and login pages. Token rotation invalidates the old refresh token for security.
   *
   * Related operations: join for initial guest registration.
   *
   * @setHeader token.access Authorization
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Refresh request containing valid refresh token for guest token renewal.
   *
   *             The refreshToken is required to validate the existing guest session and generate new authentication tokens. This token was obtained from a previous join or refresh operation.
   *
   *             Field: refreshToken (string, required) - JWT refresh token from previous join or refresh response. Must be valid, unexpired, and correspond to an active guest session in ecommerce_platform_guest_sessions.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type refresh
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor guest
   * @x-autobe-specification POST /auth/guest/refresh
   *
   * Service Logic:
   * 1. Validate refresh token structure and signature
   * 2. Decode refresh token to extract guest_id claim
   * 3. Query ecommerce_platform_guests for guest with matching id
   * 4. If guest not found or soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL): reject 401 Unauthorized
   * 5. Query ecommerce_platform_guest_sessions for valid session:
   *    - ecommerce_platform_guest_id = guest id
   *    - expired_at > current timestamp
   *    - Session tied to the refresh token
   * 6. If no valid session: reject 401 Unauthorized
   * 7. Rotate tokens: invalidate old refresh token
   * 8. Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens
   * 9. Update session record:
   *    - Set expired_at = current time + session duration (24h)
   * 10. Return IAuthorized response with new tokens
   *
   * Edge Cases:
   * - Expired session: 401 Unauthorized
   * - Invalid refresh token: 401 Unauthorized
   * - Deleted guest account: 401 Unauthorized
   * - Revoked token: 403 Forbidden
   *
   * Error Handling:
   * - 401: Invalid refresh token, expired session, or deleted guest account
   * - 403: Token revoked by administrator
   * - 500: Database error during token validation or session update
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post("refresh")
  public async refresh(
    @TypedBody()
    body: IEcommercePlatformGuest.IRefresh,
  ): Promise<IEcommercePlatformGuest.IAuthorized> {
    try {
      return await postEcommercePlatformAuthGuestRefresh({
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}
